_doc: Salvaged from ephemeral workflow transcripts by scripts/salvage-workflow-findings.mjs. These are STRUCTURED agent results — computed hypotheses (code executed against real repo files), adversarial kill verdicts, and method research. Committed because the container is ephemeral and these cost ~20M subagent tokens to produce.
_warning: A hypothesis here is NOT verified unless it carries kill verdicts from a FULL lens panel. The 2026-07-28 run reported 3 "clean survivors" that were merely UNCOVERED — their verifiers had died on a session limit and absence-of-refutation was being counted as survival. Check coverage before republishing anything from this file.

hypotheses.claim: For {N} of the {M} ingredients that carry both a sourced edible-yield figure and a certified seasonal window, the disagreement between the two independently sourced yield reference tables moves cost per usable pound by more than the entire seasonal saving the Cost Index certifies — i.e. picking the right yield number beats buying in the right month.
hypotheses.measuredResult:
N = 2 of M = 47. Kill condition (N <= 5) fires.

Only corn-on-the-cob (gap 28.6% vs save 16%, margin +12.6pp) and butternut-squash (gap 20.0% vs save 19%, margin +1.0pp). The second is a knife-edge: under a manifest-anchored denominator (|costA-costB|/costA rather than /min) butternut-squash falls to 16.7% and loses, taking N to 1. So there is exactly ONE robust case in the entire corpus.

Join: 118 yields rows x 134 depth records -> 112 slugs with both edible-yield figures non-null. The two tables agree EXACTLY (gapPct 0.0) on 66/112 (58.9%); 46/112 disagree at gapPct > 0.5.

Median gapPct among the 46 disagreeing = 8.9% (the SECOND half of the kill condition, "median below 5%", does NOT fire — where the tables disagree the disagreement is material). Max gapPct = 77.8% (octopus, manifest 0.45 vs depth 0.80).

Headline set (both yields + non-null save_pct, citrus excluded), M = 47: median save_pct = 36.0%, median gapPct = 0.0%. Only 18 of the 47 disagree at all, median gapPct among those 18 = 5.9%. Seasonal saving beats yield-source uncertainty by roughly 6x on the median.

STRUCTURAL CAUSE, verified in source: scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs:177 sets TIMING_MIN_SAVE = 15, so a seasonal window is only certified when save_pct >= 15. Observed save_pct range over the eligible set is 16..68 (min 16, median 38, max 68); zero certified windows below 15. Meanwhile only 14 of 112 joined items have gapPct > 15% at all. The comparison is structurally floored against the yield gap.

THE FLIPPED FINDING (the real result): the yield disagreement is concentrated exactly where the price instrument publishes nothing.
- By posture (non-citrus, priced 100): lock n=30, 17% disagree, max gap 20.0 | cushion n=18, 56% disagree, max 28.6 | float n=6, 67% disagree, max 12.5 | withhold n=33, 58% disagree, median gap among disagreeing 9.1, MAX 77.8.
- 25 of the 34 joined withholds have BOTH save_pct null and band_pct null - the instrument is completely silent. 15 of those 25 disagree on yield: octopus 77.8, clams 50.0, whole-crab 47.1, squid 33.3, whole-halibut 20.0, whole-lobster 20.0, collard-greens 13.8, basil 12.0, whole-trout 10.0, whole-salmon 9.1, salmon-fillet 8.0, scallops 5.3, shrimp 4.9, kale 4.5, tuna-loin 3.5.
- All 13 items with gapPct >= 20% are shellfish (6), fruiting (3), greens (2), seafood (2). ZERO in beef, meat, root, tuber, allium, herbs, mushroom, stalks - those tables agree exactly.

SECONDARY (gapPct vs band_pct, non-citrus, M=62): N = 7 exceed their band. corn-on-the-cob 28.6 vs 16.1; butternut-squash 20.0 vs 3.8; spinach 20.0 vs 19; napa-cabbage 16.3 vs 14.6; cucumber 13.1 vs 12.6; cabbage 8.8 vs 6.6; butter-lettuce 7.7 vs 5.8. Median band_pct 6.8%.

CITRUS (reported separately per spec): only 2 of the 4 citrus slugs carry a save_pct. lemon gap 7.1% vs save 40% (loses); lime gap 0.0% vs save 64% (tables agree exactly). Neither would have changed the headline.

CONFIRMED SCHEMA CLAIM: menu-pricing edible_yield_pct equals round(manifest yield * 100) on 100% of joined slugs (0 mismatches) and differs from round(depth * 100) on 39 - every published surface does silently prefer the manifest.
hypotheses.revisedClaim:
Seasonal timing dominates yield-source uncertainty for every ingredient where the Cost Index certifies a season: across the 47 ingredients carrying both a sourced edible yield and a certified seasonal window, the median certified saving is 36% of cost while the median yield-table disagreement is 0% (the two reference tables agree exactly on 66 of 112 overlapping ingredients). Only 2 ingredients invert it — corn-on-the-cob (28.6% vs 16%) and butternut-squash (20.0% vs 19%, and that one flips under a different denominator) — so the operator's cheap-month play is the larger lever wherever a cheap month exists. This is close to structural: the seasonal noise gate refuses to certify a window worth less than 15% (scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs:177), so a yield gap must clear 15% to compete, and only 14 of 112 ingredients do.

The finding that survives is the inverse one. The yield-table disagreement is concentrated precisely where the price instrument publishes nothing: 58% of withhold-posture items disagree (vs 17% of lock items), with a median gap of 9.1% and a maximum of 77.8% (octopus, 0.45 vs 0.80). For 25 of 34 joined withholds the instrument publishes neither a band nor a seasonal window, and 15 of those 25 carry a yield disagreement — octopus 77.8%, clams 50.0%, whole-crab 47.1%, squid 33.3%, whole-halibut and whole-lobster 20.0%. Every one of the 13 largest gaps is shellfish, whole fish, winter squash or a leafy green; beef, pork, roots, tubers, alliums, herbs and mushrooms agree exactly. So the Monday action is not "weigh your yields instead of chasing a cheap month" — it is "on the whole-animal seafood and whole-squash items where the public price record is silent, the yield number you picked is the only variable left, and two sourced reference tables differ on it by up to 78%."

The documented near-miss was checked explicitly: depth contains BOTH 'salmon-skin-on' AND 'salmon-skin-on-fillet' as distinct keys; the join matched only the exact string 'salmon-skin-on-fillet' and did not force-match 'salmon-skin-on'.
hypotheses.code:
import json, statistics
ROOT = "/home/user/potentially-profitable"
yields_raw = json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/data/ingredient-yields.json"))      # bare array, 118
depth      = json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/data/ingredient-depth.json"))["ingredients"]  # keyed, 134
mp = {r["slug"]: r for r in json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/cost-index/menu-pricing.json"))["ingredients"]}

y_by = {r["slug"]: r for r in yields_raw if r.get("yield") is not None}
ds   = {k for k, v in depth.items() if v.get("edibleYield") is not None}
both = sorted(set(y_by) & ds)          # exact-string join; no force-match of salmon-skin-on
CITRUS = {"lime", "lemon", "orange", "grapefruit"}

rows = []
for s in both:
    ya, yb = y_by[s]["yield"], depth[s]["edibleYield"]
    costA, costB = 1.0/ya, 1.0/yb                       # cost per usable pound, unit-free
    gap = round(100.0*abs(costA-costB)/min(costA, costB), 1)   # round BEFORE any threshold
    m = mp.get(s, {})
    rows.append(dict(slug=s, cat=y_by[s]["cat"], gapPct=gap,
                     save_pct=m.get("save_pct"), band_pct=m.get("band_pct"),
                     posture=m.get("posture"), costA=costA, costB=costB,
                     citrus=(s in CITRUS or y_by[s]["cat"] == "citrus")))

# PRIMARY
elig = [r for r in rows if r["save_pct"] is not None and not r["citrus"]]   # M = 47
wins = [r for r in elig if r["gapPct"] > r["save_pct"]]                     # N = 2
dis  = [r for r in rows if r["gapPct"] > 0.5]                               # 46 of 112
print("N =", len(wins), "M =", len(elig),
      "median gap among disagreeing =", statistics.median([r["gapPct"] for r in dis]),
      "median save =", statistics.median([r["save_pct"] for r in elig]))
print("KILL:", "FALSIFIED" if (len(wins) <= 5 or statistics.median([r["gapPct"] for r in dis]) < 5) else "SURVIVES")

# FRAGILITY: same statistic under a manifest-anchored denominator
N_man = sum(1 for r in elig if round(100*abs(r["costA"]-r["costB"])/r["costA"], 1) > r["save_pct"])
print("N under manifest denominator =", N_man)     # -> 1

# THE FLIPPED FINDING: gap by posture
for p in ("lock", "cushion", "float", "withhold"):
    g = [r for r in rows if r["posture"] == p and not r["citrus"]]
    d = [r for r in g if r["gapPct"] > 0.5]
    print(p, "n=", len(g), "disagree=", len(d),
          "medianGap(disagreeing)=", statistics.median([r["gapPct"] for r in d]),
          "max=", max(r["gapPct"] for r in g))
hypotheses.caveats:
1. NEAR-TAUTOLOGY ON THE LOW N — this is the biggest caveat and it cuts against the headline refutation being interesting. scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs:177 sets TIMING_MIN_SAVE = 15, so no seasonal window is ever certified below 15%. The observed minimum save_pct is 16. A yield gap therefore has to clear 15% just to enter contention, and only 14 of 112 joined ingredients do. The test was structurally stacked before any data was read. A fairer restatement is the one in the revised claim: the certified windows are large BY CONSTRUCTION, so "seasonal beats yield" is partly a statement about the gate's threshold, not purely about the world.

2. FRAGILITY — N=2 collapses to N=1 under an equally defensible denominator. The spec fixed |costA-costB|/min(costA,costB); anchoring instead on costA (the manifest, which is what every published Muntin surface actually uses) drops butternut-squash from 20.0% to 16.7%, below its 19% saving. Butternut's winning margin under the specced denominator is +1.0pp. Leave-one-out on that single ingredient halves N. Only corn-on-the-cob survives both specifications.

3. THIS IS NOT MEASUREMENT ERROR, IT IS TWO BOOKS DISAGREEING. Neither yield figure is an observation. data/ingredient-yields.json is pinned to the CIA/USDA YIELD_TABLE in tools/plate-cost/plate-cost.js (drift-gated by scripts/check-ingredient-yields.mjs); data/ingredient-depth.json is sourced to US Foods / extension-service references with per-row yieldConfidence. gapPct is an arithmetic consequence of two reference-book numbers, not a measured price effect and not evidence that either book is wrong. Nothing here says which table is right, and neither reflects Don's kitchen.

4. THE WITHHOLD CONCENTRATION MAY BE PARTLY A SOURCING ARTIFACT, NOT A MARKET FACT. The 16 no_series withholds are almost all whole-animal seafood — exactly the items where "edible yield" is definitionally contested (head-on vs headed, shell-in vs picked, gutted vs whole). Octopus at 0.45 vs 0.80 may reflect two different cut specs rather than a genuine disagreement about the same operation. I did NOT verify that the two tables define the same cut for the divergent items; depth carries a cutSpec field that would need reading per-slug to settle it. Treat the shellfish/whole-fish cluster as "the two tables may not be measuring the same knife," structurally analogous to the citrus juice-yield carve-out the spec already excluded.

5. SURVIVORSHIP CHECKED AND CLEAN. save_pct is non-null on only 49 of the 90 priced-100 joined items, so 41 are excluded by the noise gate. Their gap distribution is identical to the included set (median 0.0% both), so the headline is not distorted by which ingredients earned a certified window. Similarly, items inside vs outside the priced 100 both have median gap 0.0%.

6. NO UNITS ENTERED THE COMPUTATION, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THAT WENT RIGHT. gapPct, save_pct and band_pct are all percent-of-cost, so the carton/lb/sack/dozen trap (65 of 100 slugs trade by carton, and the unit lives only in a different file) is fully avoided. No cents value, no medianCents, no epCents, and no delivered-price claim is anywhere in this result. Consistent with the honesty contract: nothing here is a price, a forecast, or a cause.

7. PRIOR ART THAT MUST BE CITED IF THIS PUBLISHES. USDA ERS Fruit and Vegetable Prices already joins edible-yield factors to prices — at RETAIL (Circana scanner data, latest pricing 2022), annually, per edible cup equivalent, for household cost-per-serving. The novel part here is the wholesale/operator framing and the disagreement-between-two-tables angle, not the price x yield join itself.

8. MULTIPLICITY. This is one pre-specified hypothesis with a pre-stated kill condition, tested once, against a fixed corpus. No search over specifications was performed beyond the single declared denominator-sensitivity check, which is reported above rather than selected on. But the enumerated denominator is 112 ingredients and I report per-ingredient winners; the two named winners are the max of 47 comparisons and should be treated accordingly.

hypotheses.claim: Named culinary substitutes co-move MORE than category-matched non-substitute pairs — the shared-episode rate for the {n} substitute pairs is {X}% against {Y}% for controls drawn from the same ingredient category — meaning the standard trade advice 'swap to the cheaper one' is systematically weaker as a hedge than it is assumed to be.
hypotheses.measuredResult:
PRIMARY (pre-specified design: min 3 eligible controls, cap 20 per stratum, seed 20260730).
- Treatment: 30 named-substitute pairs. Mean averaged shared-episode fraction = 0.26944 (26.94%).
- Control: 251 category-matched non-substitute pairs across those 30 strata. Mean of per-stratum control means = 0.09772 (9.77%); pooled control mean = 0.11262 (11.26%).
- Difference (treatment - matched control) = +0.17173 (+17.17 percentage points). Ratio = 2.757x.
- Share with any shared episode (>0): treatment 20 of 30 = 66.7%; control 123 of 251 = 49.0%. Median treatment 0.16667; median control 0.00000.
- Permutation null, 10,000 iterations, substitute label shuffled within each category-matched stratum: 0 of 10,000 null draws reached the observed difference. Null mean +0.000121, null sd 0.032391. ONE-SIDED p = 0.0001. Per-stratum midrank of the treatment pair = 0.689 (0.5 = null); treatment beat its stratum mean in 19 strata, lost in 7.
KILL CONDITION NOT MET (treatment > control, and p < 0.05).

ROBUSTNESS (6 variants, all in the same direction):
- Relax to min 1 control, all eligible controls, no cap (38 pairs, 263 controls): 23.90% vs 11.79%, +12.11pp, p = 0.0005. This restores the 8 pairs dropped for thin control pools (lemon/lime, ribeye/striploin, broccoli/cauliflower, onion/red-onion, cilantro/parsley, leek/onion, broccoli/brussels-sprouts, brussels-sprouts/cabbage), whose exclusion was outcome-correlated.
- Seed stability: identical results across 5 seeds (every eligible pool was at or under the cap of 20, so no sampling actually occurred).
- Leave-one-category-out (10 categories): survives all ten. Weakest is dropping 'greens' (n=27): +8.10pp, p = 0.0133. Strongest is dropping 'cruciferous': +15.92pp, p = 0.0001.
- One pair per distinct anchor (kills pseudo-replication; 30 strata came from only 23 distinct anchors): 21.39% vs 11.09%, +10.30pp, p = 0.0026.

THE DECISIVE SPLIT — the effect is entirely same-category:
- Same-category substitute pairs (n=32): 26.82% vs 12.28% for same-category controls, +14.54pp, p = 0.0001.
- Cross-category substitute pairs (n=6): 8.33% vs 9.20% for their controls, -0.87pp, p = 0.4503. INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM CONTROL. n=6 is far too small to conclude anything either way.
- Unmatched background across all 3,160 anchor pairs: mean 0.0535 (5.35%), 770 of 3,160 = 24.4% share any episode. Category matching absorbs roughly half of the raw treatment-vs-background gap, which is exactly the confound the control was built for.

TOP 10 MOST-ENTANGLED SUBSTITUTE PAIRS (the fake hedges), averaged fraction:
chicken breast<->chicken thigh 0.917 (5/6 and 5/5); green-leaf<->iceberg lettuce 0.667; green-leaf<->red-leaf lettuce 0.667; iceberg<->romaine 0.667; broccoli<->cauliflower 0.500; butter-leaf<->green-leaf 0.500; butter-leaf<->red-leaf 0.500; cherry tomato<->tomato 0.500; cucumber<->zucchini 0.500; green-leaf<->romaine 0.500.

ZERO SHARED EPISODES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — 16 of the 39 scoreable pairs: cabbage<->iceberg lettuce, whole chicken<->whole turkey, asparagus<->green beans, apple<->pear, lemon<->lime, brussels sprouts<->cabbage, bok choy<->cabbage, leek<->onion, cilantro<->parsley, butternut squash<->pumpkin, pork belly<->pork shoulder, broccoli<->brussels sprouts, cabbage<->napa cabbage, bok choy<->napa cabbage, chicken thigh<->whole chicken, bell pepper<->poblano pepper.

TAUTOLOGY CHECK (passed): treatment was defined by `subSlug` (the hand-authored culinary substitute list), NOT by the repo's `hedge` verdict, which the file's own _doc states is "computed from our own co-movement data" and would be circular. Cross-check confirms the circularity of that field: pairs the repo labels 'mirror' average 0.568 (n=11), 'hedge' average 0.079 (n=36).
hypotheses.revisedClaim: Among the 30 named culinary substitute pairs that can be scored, the mean shared-episode fraction is 26.9% against 9.8% for 251 category-matched non-substitute control pairs — a 2.8x gap (permutation one-sided p = 0.0001, 0 of 10,000 null draws). The gap survives restoring the thin-pool pairs (+12.1pp, p = 0.0005), every leave-one-category-out variant (weakest +8.1pp, p = 0.0133), and collapsing to one pair per anchor (+10.3pp, p = 0.0026). But it is carried entirely by SAME-category substitutes: 32 same-category pairs run 26.8% against 12.3% for same-category controls (p = 0.0001), while the 6 cross-category substitute pairs run 8.3% against 9.2% for their controls (p = 0.45) — no detectable difference, on a sample far too small to license a rule. The operator-facing version: a named substitute drawn from the same category is about 2.8 times more likely to share this ingredient's price episodes than a random item from that same category, so the swap is weakest exactly where it is most natural to reach — chicken breast to chicken thigh sits at 0.92, and five of the ten most entangled pairs are lettuce varieties. Meanwhile 16 of the 39 scoreable substitute pairs shared zero episodes in both directions, including lemon<->lime, leek<->onion, apple<->pear and bell pepper<->poblano. This is shared timing within a ~6-week window over each ingredient's own detected episodes — co-occurrence, never a correlation coefficient, never a lead/lag, never a cause.

hypotheses.code:
import json, random, statistics
from collections import defaultdict
ROOT = "/home/user/potentially-profitable"
cm    = json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/cost-index/co-movement.json"))["anchors"]
depth = json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/data/ingredient-depth.json"))["ingredients"]
CAT   = {r["slug"]: r["category"]
         for r in json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/cost-index/menu-pricing.json"))["ingredients"]}

# directed shared-episode fraction; absence in neighbors is a REAL ZERO, not missing
K = {(a, nb): k for a, r in cm.items() for nb, k in r["neighbors"]}
def cdir(a, b):
    if a not in cm or not cm[a]["n"]: return None      # no episodes -> undefined, not 0
    return K.get((a, b), 0) / cm[a]["n"]
def cavg(a, b):
    x, y = cdir(a, b), cdir(b, a)
    return None if x is None or y is None else (x + y) / 2.0

# TREATMENT: hand-authored culinary substitutes (subSlug), NOT the circular `hedge` field
declared = set()
for s, rec in depth.items():
    for sub in (rec.get("substitutes") or []):
        ss = sub.get("subSlug")
        if ss and ss != s: declared.add(tuple(sorted((s, ss))))
treat = [(a, b, cavg(a, b)) for a, b in sorted(declared) if cavg(a, b) is not None]  # 39

# CONTROLS: same category as the SUBSTITUTE, in anchor space, not a declared substitute of a
by_cat = defaultdict(list)
for s in cm:
    if CAT.get(s): by_cat[CAT[s]].append(s)
random.seed(20260730)
strata = []
for a, b, tv in treat:
    cb = CAT.get(b)
    if not cb: continue
    elig = [(c, cavg(a, c)) for c in sorted(by_cat[cb])
            if c not in (a, b)
            and tuple(sorted((a, c))) not in declared
            and cavg(a, c) is not None]
    if len(elig) < 3: continue                              # MIN_CTRL; 8 pairs dropped
    strata.append({"t": tv, "ctrl": elig if len(elig) <= 20 else random.sample(elig, 20)})

t   = [s["t"] for s in strata]
cpm = [statistics.mean(v for _, v in s["ctrl"]) for s in strata]
obs = statistics.mean(t) - statistics.mean(cpm)

# stratified permutation: shuffle which member of each matched pool wears the 'substitute' label
pools = [[s["t"]] + [v for _, v in s["ctrl"]] for s in strata]
ge = 0
for _ in range(10000):
    dt = dc = 0.0
    for pool in pools:
        i = random.randrange(len(pool))
        dt += pool[i]
        rest = pool[:i] + pool[i+1:]
        dc  += sum(rest) / len(rest)
    if (dt - dc) / len(pools) >= obs: ge += 1

print(len(t), statistics.mean(t), statistics.mean(cpm), obs, (ge + 1) / 10001)
# -> 30  0.26944  0.09772  +0.17173  p=0.0001
hypotheses.caveats:
SMALL n, SAID LOUDLY. The primary test is 30 treatment pairs from only 23 distinct anchor ingredients. The cross-category arm — the half of the operator rule that says "pick your backup from a different category" — is n=6 and is statistically empty (p=0.45). It does not support that rule; it merely fails to contradict it. Do not publish the "different category" half as a finding.

SHARED REPORTING, NOT NECESSARILY SHARED MARKET. Episodes are detected from the same deep history built on USDA AMS terminal-market prints, and the 8 AMS terminal markets are ONE methodology, not independent corroboration. Green-leaf, red-leaf, butter and iceberg lettuce are reported on the same reports out of the same shipping districts. Five of the ten most-entangled pairs are lettuce varieties. A "shared episode" between two varieties of the same commodity may be substantially a shared-collection artifact rather than two markets moving together. Nothing in these three files can separate the two.

SEVERE COVERAGE LOSS / SURVIVORSHIP. 42 of 81 declared substitute pairs (51.9%) are unscoreable because at least one member has no detected episode — 20 of the responsible slugs are not in the priced corpus at all. The result speaks only to substitute pairs where both ingredients have a detectable episode history. Controls are drawn from the same conditioned space, so the contrast is internally valid, but the treatment set is not a random sample of the culinary substitute universe.

COARSE DENOMINATOR. The events builder caps detection at topN=6 episodes per ingredient, and 65 of 80 anchors sit at exactly n=6, so k/n moves in steps of 0.167. Four of the 39 treatment pairs involve a member with n<=2, where the fraction can only be 0 or 1. Effect sizes are lumpy by construction.

NON-INDEPENDENCE. Strata share anchors (green-leaf lettuce appears 3 times; apple, asparagus, bok choy, butter lettuce twice each). The permutation treats strata as independent, which is optimistic. The one-pair-per-anchor variant addresses it and the effect survives at +10.30pp, p=0.0026 — roughly 40% smaller than the headline, which is the honest magnitude.

DROP RULE WAS OUTCOME-CORRELATED. The pre-specified "fewer than 3 eligible controls -> drop" rule removed 8 pairs sitting in the narrowest categories (citrus, beef, cruciferous, allium, herbs) — precisely where the closest substitutes live, and including three of the zero-comovement pairs. Restoring them cuts the effect from +17.17pp to +12.11pp. The +12.11pp figure is the more defensible headline; the +17.17pp is the artifact of a rule that happened to discard low-scoring treatment pairs.

TAUTOLOGY AVOIDED BUT WORTH NAMING. The repo's own `hedge`/`mirror` verdict IS derived from this same co-movement file and using it as treatment would have been circular (mirror pairs average 0.568, hedge pairs 0.079 — that is definitional, not a finding). The treatment set here is the independent culinary substitute list. Residual risk: that list was authored inside a repo where the co-movement data already existed, so soft authoring contamination cannot be ruled out from the files alone.

UNITS AND VOCABULARY. k/n is a bounded co-occurrence fraction inside a ~6-week window, directed and asymmetric (the denominator is each anchor's own episode count), computed over nominal cents per package unit with no inflation adjustment across a 25-year event span. It is not a correlation coefficient, not a lead/lag, not a magnitude, and not a cause. Any published sentence must use shared-timing vocabulary and carry the co-occurrence caveat.

MULTIPLICITY NOT ACCOUNTED. This is one pre-specified test with a pre-stated direction and executable kill condition, so no within-test correction applies. But it is one hypothesis among many enumerated by the surrounding discovery engine; the engine-level FDR denominator is not reflected in the p reported here. A p of 0.0001 against a stratified permutation null is comfortably robust to a moderate denominator, but the +8.10pp / p=0.0133 leave-greens-out variant is not.

hypotheses.revisedClaim: In the Muntin 100-ingredient catalog, "no-series" darkness is not a supply signature — it is a category boundary. All 15 seafood/shellfish slugs are withheld for no-series and zero appear in any published bucket, so the no-series set is 15 seafood plus ground-beef by construction, and "dark vs published" cannot be distinguished from "seafood vs land agriculture" in this corpus. Measured: median import-source HHI is 0.310 for no-series (n=16) vs 0.645 for volatile (n=10), permutation p=0.0169 — but collapsing the 4 pseudo-replicate slugs that share an HS6 code with an identical HHI (shrimp/shrimp-head-on at 0.30; salmon-fillet/salmon-skin-on-fillet at 0.45) to 12 product families raises the no-series median to 0.375 and the p to 0.1013, so the volatile-vs-no-series split does not survive de-replication. The "no attribute separates" arm is refuted outright: HHI separates no-series (0.310) from published (0.590) at BH-adjusted p=0.0244 — though that separation is entirely a Mexico effect, since 30 of 53 published slugs source #1 from Mexico at median HHI 0.71 and against the 23 non-Mexico published slugs (median 0.38) the no-series set does not separate (p=0.2713). Two of the four pre-specified attributes were uncomputable because the public record structurally withholds them for the dark set: import_reliance_pct is present on 1 of 16 no-series slugs versus 46 of 63 published, and us_percap_lbs on 1 of 16 versus 47 of 63, with ground-beef the only non-null in both. Finally the "exotic, low-trade" intuition is inverted rather than merely wrong: the no-series set carries the highest median import value of any subgroup ($862,960,860 vs $119,699,128 for published), led by ground-beef at $5.34B and shrimp-pd at $3.32B. The honest operator-facing statement is narrower than the original: a no-series ingredient is dark because no US agency publishes a wholesale reference for that product class, and in this catalog that class is wild-caught and imported seafood — not because it is obscure, low-volume, or single-sourced.

hypotheses.code:
import json, random, statistics as st
random.seed(20260730); NPERM=10000; ROOT="/home/user/potentially-profitable"
lf=json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/data/cost-lockfloat.json"))
isr=json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/cost-index/ingredient-state-record.json"))
items=lf["items"]; rec={r["slug"]:r for r in isr["ingredients"]}
G={"NOSERIES":[],"VOLATILE":[],"FLAT":[],"PUBLISHED":[]}
for s,it in items.items():
    if it["bucket"]!="withhold": G["PUBLISHED"].append(s)
    else: G[{"no-series":"NOSERIES","volatile":"VOLATILE","flat":"FLAT"}[it["reason"]]].append(s)
med=lambda x: st.median(x) if x else None
vals=lambda g,f:[rec[s][f] for s in g if rec[s].get(f) is not None]
F="import_source_hhi"

# ---- ARM 1: permutation on the median difference, nulls travel with the unit
def perm_med(pool,nA,obs):
    hits=0; idx=list(range(len(pool)))
    for _ in range(NPERM):
        random.shuffle(idx)
        va=vals([pool[i] for i in idx[:nA]],F); vb=vals([pool[i] for i in idx[nA:]],F)
        if va and vb and abs(med(vb)-med(va))>=obs-1e-12: hits+=1
    return hits/NPERM
ns,vo=vals(G["NOSERIES"],F),vals(G["VOLATILE"],F)          # 0.310 vs 0.645
p1=perm_med(G["NOSERIES"]+G["VOLATILE"],16,abs(med(vo)-med(ns)))   # 0.0169

# ---- ARM 2: Wilcoxon rank-sum (mid-ranks) with a permutation null
def ranksum(a,b):
    pooled=sorted([(v,0) for v in a]+[(v,1) for v in b]); ranks=[0.0]*len(pooled); i=0
    while i<len(pooled):
        j=i
        while j+1<len(pooled) and pooled[j+1][0]==pooled[i][0]: j+=1
        for k in range(i,j+1): ranks[k]=(i+j)/2.0+1.0
        i=j+1
    return sum(r for r,(v,g) in zip(ranks,pooled) if g==0)
def perm_rs(a,b):
    obs=ranksum(a,b); pooled=a+b; na=len(a)
    mean=na*(len(pooled)+1)/2.0; dev=abs(obs-mean); hits=0; idx=list(range(len(pooled)))
    for _ in range(NPERM):
        random.shuffle(idx)
        if abs(ranksum([pooled[i] for i in idx[:na]],[pooled[i] for i in idx[na:]])-mean)>=dev-1e-9: hits+=1
    return hits/NPERM
def dedupe_hs6(g):                       # one representative per distinct import_hs6
    seen,out=set(),[]
    for s in sorted(g):
        h=rec[s].get("import_hs6")
        if h is None: out.append(s); continue
        if h in seen: continue
        seen.add(h); out.append(s)
    return out
raw={}
for f in ["import_source_hhi","import_reliance_pct","us_percap_lbs","us_import_value_usd"]:
    gA,gB=(dedupe_hs6(G["NOSERIES"]),dedupe_hs6(G["PUBLISHED"])) if f=="us_import_value_usd" \
          else (G["NOSERIES"],G["PUBLISHED"])
    a,b=vals(gA,f),vals(gB,f)
    raw[f]=perm_rs(a,b) if (len(a)>=2 and len(b)>=2) else None   # reliance/percap -> None (n=1)
# BH over the m=4 declared tests -> hhi raw .0061 adj .0244 SIG ; import value .1207 adj .2414 ns

# ---- de-replication robustness: collapse shrimp/salmon families (16 -> 12 units)
SP={"shrimp":["shrimp","shrimp-pd","shrimp-head-on"],
    "salmon":["salmon-fillet","salmon-skin-on-fillet","whole-salmon"]}
col,used=[],set()
for fam,m in SP.items():
    ms=[x for x in m if x in G["NOSERIES"]]
    if ms: col.append(ms[0]); used.update(ms)
col+=[s for s in G["NOSERIES"] if s not in used]
p1c=perm_med(col+G["VOLATILE"],len(col),abs(med(vo)-med(vals(col,F))))  # 0.1013
p2c=perm_rs(vals(col,F),vals(G["PUBLISHED"],F))                        # 0.0466 -> BH .1864

# ---- confound: seafood is perfectly collinear with no-series
SEA={"seafood","shellfish"}
assert all(items[s]["reason"]=="no-series" for s in items if rec[s].get("category") in SEA)  # 15/15
nonmex=[s for s in G["PUBLISHED"] if (rec[s].get("import_top_sources") or [{}])[0].get("country") not in (None,"Mexico")]
p_nonmex=perm_rs(ns,vals(nonmex,F))    # 0.2713 ; collapsed 0.5279
hypotheses.caveats:
SAMPLE SIZES ARE VERY SMALL AND THIS IS THE DOMINANT LIMITATION. NOSERIES n=16, VOLATILE n=10, FLAT n=11. Permutation distributions of a median difference at n=10 are lumpy and discrete; the ARM-1 p of 0.0169 rests on 26 units, four of which are duplicates of two others.

DEFINITIONAL COLLINEARITY (fatal to the mechanism claim). All 15 seafood/shellfish slugs in the catalog are no-series and none appear in any published bucket, so the NOSERIES group IS the seafood group plus ground-beef. Any attribute on which seafood differs from produce/meat will "separate" no-series from published. The design cannot distinguish "darkness has a supply signature" from "seafood has a supply signature," and no re-analysis of these two files can, because the corpus contains zero published seafood.

NEAR-TAUTOLOGY. The lockfloat 'no-series' reason means no deep public wholesale series exists. USDA AMS/LMR covers land agriculture; NOAA publishes ex-vessel landings value, not wholesale prices. Which agency covers which product class is knowable a priori, so this test can confirm the institutional story but cannot discover it. The "institutional not economic" framing is closer to a restatement of the corpus construction than to an empirical result.

PSEUDO-REPLICATION. The pre-specified ARM 1 and ARM 2 treated shrimp/shrimp-head-on (shared HS 030617, identical HHI 0.30) and salmon-fillet/salmon-skin-on-fillet (shared HS 030441, identical HHI 0.45) as independent units. They are the same trade stream. The pre-registered test therefore over-counted effective n by 4 of 16; de-replication moves ARM 1 from p=0.0169 to p=0.1013 and ARM 2 from BH-adj 0.0244 to 0.1864. I report the pre-specified result as primary per the spec, but the de-replicated result is the more defensible one.

ALREADY-PUBLISHED CONTEXT, NOT NOVEL. The driver of the ARM-2 "separation" is that US produce imports are Mexico-concentrated while seafood imports are spread across India, Ecuador, Chile, Canada, Indonesia, Argentina, Norway, Spain and Japan. USDA ERS already publishes the produce side (Mexico supplied roughly half of fresh fruit and about two-thirds of fresh vegetable import value in 2023). This should be attributed, not claimed.

VALUE, NOT VOLUME OR SUPPLY. us_import_value_usd is nominal customs general-import value in whole dollars, undeflated, mixing price and quantity; HS6 does not publish quantity. It is not a supply measure and not a delivered price. import_source_hhi, import_reliance_pct and the concentration labels are Muntin-derived, not published statistics; import_source_hhi is computed over all source countries while only the top 3 are visible in the record, so hhi and the visible top-3 are not reconcilable row by row.

DIFFERENTIAL MISSINGNESS. import_source_hhi is non-null on 16/16 NOSERIES but only 53/63 PUBLISHED, so the two groups are not equally observed even on the one attribute that tested significant. For reliance and per-capita the asymmetry is near-total (1/16 vs 46/63 and 1/16 vs 47/63); those two members of the declared family were not tested at all, so ARM 2's "no attribute separates" was in practice evaluated on 2 attributes, not 4. BH was still applied over m=4 as declared, which is conservative in the correct direction. Note that the missingness pattern itself is an enormous separator, but it was not one of the four pre-specified continuous tests and I did not convert it into one.

SURVIVORSHIP / SELECTION. The 100-slug catalog is the set Muntin chose to track, and seafood was included knowing it had no wholesale series. The subgroup sizes are a product of that curation, not of a random sample of US food products.

MULTIPLICITY BEYOND THIS FAMILY. The BH correction covers only the 4 declared attributes in this hypothesis. It does not cover the other hypotheses in the wider discovery run; the run-level denominator is not reflected in these adjusted p-values.

REPRODUCIBILITY. Single seed (20260730), 10,000 permutations per test; Monte Carlo standard error on a p near 0.02 is roughly 0.0013, so the reported p-values are stable to the third decimal but were not re-run across multiple seeds.

hypotheses.claim: Across the tracked record, how LONG a large wholesale episode takes to clear is roughly invariant to how predictable the ingredient is, even though how BIG the episode is is not: median durationDays differs by no more than {D} days across the four lock/cushion/float/withhold classes (observed spread ~14 days on a ~77-day median), while median pctFromNormal differs by a factor of {M} across the same classes (observed ~3.7x, 45% to 167%).
hypotheses.measuredResult:
DETECTOR VALIDATION FIRST: my re-implementation of build-cost-index-events.mjs reproduced 432/432 shipped events exactly (date, durationDays, pctFromNormal), so the sweep is trustworthy.

ANALYSIS SET: 412 events across 76 slugs. From 420 joined events I dropped 7 with basis==='index' (pork-belly, vegetable-oil; their durations were 275/305/273/304/426/123/152, median 275d) and 1 with durationDays>365 (dill 2007-03-29, 4243d). The dill 4243d event survived the index filter; the 426d vegetable-oil event was already removed by the index filter, so only 1 long event was dropped by the >365 rule, not 2.

STATISTIC A — durationDays by bucket (median / Hodges-Lehmann / n events / n slugs):
  lock     70 / 73.5 / n=174 / 35 slugs
  cushion  70 / 77.0 / n=113 / 19 slugs
  float    80.5 / 84.0 / n=42 / 7 slugs
  withhold 84 / 80.5 / n=83 / 15 slugs
  Pooled median 77 days, IQR 50.75–98.
  Max pairwise |median difference| = 14.0 days (ratio 1.200x).
  Slug-level permutation test, 10,000 draws: p = 0.5304. The observed spread of 14 sits EXACTLY at the null median (14); the null 95th percentile is 24.5. Duration is statistically indistinguishable from random bucket assignment.
  Cluster bootstrap (4,000 draws, resample slugs within bucket): 95% CI on the max pairwise gap = [3.5, 28] days.

STATISTIC B — |pctFromNormal| by bucket (median / HL):
  lock     47.5 / 54.0
  cushion  95.0 / 100.5
  float    158.5 / 170.0
  withhold 128.0 / 136.5
  Max pairwise |median difference| = 111 pct-points; max/min ratio = 3.337x.
  Permutation test, same design, 10,000 draws: p = 0.0105 (null median spread 38, null 95th 79).

KILL CONDITION 1 (duration p<0.05 AND stable ordering): NOT MET. p=0.5304.

KILL CONDITION 2 (duration medians collapse onto mergeWeeks, slope ~7 d per merge-week): NOT MET. Re-ran the detector with topN=Infinity over the 9-cell grid mergeWeeks∈{6,12,24} × floorPct∈{15,20,30}. Pooled median duration vs mergeWeeks slope: floorPct=15 → +0.417 d/merge-week (56/56/63); floorPct=20 → +0.012 (56/55/56); floorPct=30 → 0.000 (49/49/49). This is mechanically expected: durationDays is computed by shoulder expansion from the peak (shoulder = FLOOR_PCT*SHOULDER_FRAC/100) and never reads MERGE_WEEKS. Duration DOES depend on floorPct by construction (pooled 56→56→49 as floor goes 15→20→30), as it must.

FULL 9-CELL GRID (topN=Inf; lock/cushion/float/withhold median duration, spread, permutation p at 2,000 draws):
  mw=6,fp=15:  70/49/49/56, spread 21, p=0.220
  mw=6,fp=20:  70/49/49/49, spread 21, p=0.211
  mw=6,fp=30:  63/42/42/49, spread 21, p=0.183
  mw=12,fp=15: 63.5/50.5/49/56, spread 14.5, p=0.106
  mw=12,fp=20: 63/49/49/49, spread 14, p=0.345
  mw=12,fp=30: 56/42/42/49, spread 14, p=0.444
  mw=24,fp=15: 70/56/56/56, spread 14, p=0.512
  mw=24,fp=20: 70/53/49/56, spread 21, p=0.130
  mw=24,fp=30: 63/49/49/56, spread 14, p=0.487
  0 of 9 cells reach p<0.05. Spread stays in a tight 14–21 day band everywhere.

AN ARTIFACT THE HYPOTHESIS DID NOT GUARD AGAINST — AND IT IS REAL: the "~77-day / ~11-week" constant is an artifact of topN=6, not of mergeWeeks. Holding floorPct=20 and mergeWeeks=12 and varying only the per-ingredient cap: top-1 → 84d (n=76), top-3 → 77d (n=217), top-6 → 77d (n=412), top-12 → 70d (n=765), top-25 → 63d (n=1408), ALL → 55d (n=2583). Uncapped, 2,583 episodes exist versus the 412 shipped. So "~11 weeks" describes the six biggest episodes per ingredient, not episodes. The 14-day BUCKET SPREAD, by contrast, is stable at exactly 14 days across top-3, top-6, top-12, top-25 and top-ALL.

ORDERING IS UNSTABLE AND REVERSES: shipped config ranks withhold longest (84) and lock shortest (70). In all 9 full-enumeration sweep cells LOCK is longest (63–70) and cushion/float shortest (42–56) — a 9/9 vote in the opposite direction. No stable ordering exists, which supports invariance but forbids any directional read.

EVENT-LEVEL CORRELATIONS: Spearman rho(|pctFromNormal|, durationDays) = +0.1581 (n=412) — size and duration are weakly positively linked at the event level, but it does not aggregate into a bucket difference. Spearman rho(deep-series length, durationDays) = +0.1097.

PROPOSER'S NUMBERS DID NOT ALL REPRODUCE: the duration figures (14-day spread, 77-day median) reproduce exactly. The magnitude figures do not — observed is 47.5%→158.5% and 3.337x, not "45% to 167%" and 3.7x. Without any exclusions the numbers are 46/95/158.5/128 and 3.446x; neither variant yields 3.7x.
hypotheses.revisedClaim: Among the 412 largest detected wholesale episodes across 76 tracked ingredients, episode DURATION does not sort by conformal predictability class while episode SIZE does. Median durationDays is 70 (lock), 70 (cushion), 80.5 (float) and 84 (withhold) — a 14-day maximum gap on a 77-day pooled median, which is exactly the median gap produced by shuffling the class labels at random (slug-level permutation, 10,000 draws, p=0.53; cluster-bootstrap 95% CI on the gap [3.5, 28] days). Median |pctFromNormal| over the same events is 47.5%, 95%, 158.5% and 128% — a 3.34x span, p=0.011. The duration null is not a merge-window artifact: re-running the detector with topN removed across mergeWeeks∈{6,12,24} × floorPct∈{15,20,30}, the pooled duration median moves 0.0–0.4 days per merge-week, the bucket spread stays inside 14–21 days, and none of the 9 cells reaches p<0.05. THREE MATERIAL QUALIFICATIONS. (1) The "~11 weeks" figure is a top-6 truncation artifact: uncapped, 2,583 episodes exist and the pooled median is 55 days, sliding monotonically 84→77→70→63→55 as the per-ingredient cap widens from 1 to unlimited. The stable quantity is the ~14-day BETWEEN-CLASS gap, not the 77-day level. (2) The ordering reverses between configurations — withhold is longest in the shipped file, lock is longest in all 9 uncapped sweep cells — so "which class is longest" has no answer. (3) The magnitude half is near-tautological, as the proposer conceded: the lock/cushion/float/withhold label is assigned from a conformal half-width computed over the same deep history the episodes are detected in, so a wider band mechanically implies larger departures. The only non-tautological result here is the duration null, and it is a null with modest power: float rests on 7 slugs and withhold on 15 of its 37 (22 contribute nothing — 16 have no deep series at all and 6 are degenerate-flat).

hypotheses.caveats:
1. POWER IS WEAK AND THE HEADLINE IS A NULL. float rests on 7 slugs / 42 events; withhold on 15 slugs / 83 events. A 14-day gap is what random labels produce (null median = 14, null 95th = 24.5), but "indistinguishable from noise" is not "equal." The cluster bootstrap puts the true gap anywhere in [3.5, 28] days — the data cannot rule out a real 4-week difference. The claim's "no more than {D} days" should be stated as 28, not 14.

2. THE topN=6 ARTIFACT IS REAL AND THE HYPOTHESIS GUARDED AGAINST THE WRONG PARAMETER. The proposer correctly worried the ~77-day constant might be manufactured, but pointed at mergeWeeks=12 (84 days). mergeWeeks is innocent — durationDays is computed by shoulder expansion and never reads it (slope 0.0–0.4 d/merge-week, measured). The real cap is topN=6: uncapped there are 2,583 episodes with a 55-day pooled median. Any published "~11 weeks to clear" would be a statement about the six biggest episodes per ingredient. The between-class gap (14 days) survives the cap; the level (77 days) does not.

3. THE MAGNITUDE HALF IS CIRCULAR, NOT A FINDING. lockfloat bucket = conformal half-width of a walk-forward band computed over data/cost-index-history.json; pctFromNormal = departure from a ±26-week local median of the SAME series. Wider band ⇒ larger departures, by construction. p=0.0105 is measuring a definitional relationship. This is a lookup, not a discovery, and should never be published as one.

4. WITHHOLD IS NOT ONE POPULATION. Of 37 withhold slugs, 16 ('no-series') can never produce an event — they have no deep history at all — and 6 more ('flat') produce none. The bucket's 84-day median rests on 15 slugs that split cleanly into 10 'volatile' (duration 84, |pct| 180.5) and 5 'flat' (duration 77, |pct| 51). Pooling them is a category error the public cost-index/lockfloat.json cannot even detect, since it strips `reason`.

5. SURVIVORSHIP: only ingredients with ≥52 weekly observations (2*BASE_WIN) can generate any event, and only 76 of 100 joined slugs contribute. The seafood complex is almost entirely absent. Nothing here generalizes to the ingredients the instrument already declines to band.

6. ORDERING IS NOT STABLE — IT REVERSES. Shipped: withhold longest. All 9 uncapped sweep cells: lock longest, 9/9. This is consistent with there being no signal, but it also means no directional statement ("volatile items clear slower") is supportable in either direction.

7. UNITS: durationDays is days and is cadence-agnostic; pctFromNormal is a WHOLE INTEGER PERCENT (183 = +183%), not a fraction, and I used |pctFromNormal| for magnitude since 376 of 412 events are 'up'. No cents figure was used anywhere, so the per-package-unit trap does not apply. Nominal, undeflated, spanning 2001–2026 — a 2001 departure and a 2026 departure are compared in percent-from-own-local-normal terms, which is inflation-neutral by construction, but the 26-week local normal is the only deflator.

8. NOT INDEPENDENT TESTS. The 9 sweep cells are nested parameter settings over one dataset, not 9 independent replications; their p-values should not be combined. The two headline permutation tests share the same 412 events. No multiplicity correction was applied across the two statistics.

9. CO-OCCURRENCE ONLY. Nothing here establishes that predictability class causes (or fails to cause) episode length. Both quantities are Muntin-derived from the same public price history.

hypotheses.revisedClaim: Across the 72 tracked ingredients carrying both a reliance figure and a source-concentration figure, import reliance and import-source concentration are statistically independent: Spearman rho = +0.085 (95% bootstrap CI [-0.157, +0.325], permutation p = 0.48), and on the item-scope subset alone — the only rows that are genuinely independent observations — rho = +0.013 (p = 0.94). The panel is large enough to rule out any association of |rho| ≥ 0.33. Thirteen ingredients sit in the joint high-high corner (reliance ≥ 75% AND HHI ≥ 0.50) — brussels sprouts, papaya, pineapple, avocado, cucumber, raspberry, the five peppers, and the two tomatoes, 12 of 13 sourced primarily from Mexico — but that is NOT a small number: independence predicts 12.2, and the observed 13 gives an odds ratio of 1.26 with Fisher p = 0.79, holding across all 20 reliance x HHI threshold combinations tested. The correct correction to the intuitive story is therefore NOT that these are "two mostly-different sets of ingredients" — 65% of high-reliance ingredients are also concentrated. It is that concentration is simply common in this panel (44 of 72, 61%), so high-reliance ingredients are concentrated at essentially the base rate (65% vs 61%, lift 1.06x). Knowing an ingredient is import-reliant tells you almost nothing about whether its imports are concentrated that the base rate did not already tell you. A single multiplicative "supply risk" score is the wrong shape because the two axes carry independent information, not because they pick out disjoint ingredients. Methodological finding of equal weight: the commodity-scope subset alone appears to show a real association (rho = +0.363, p = 0.031), but this is entirely an artifact of one group-level reliance number being stamped onto every member slug — those 35 rows carry only 11 distinct reliance values, and collapsing to the 11 independent groups returns rho = +0.146 (p = 0.67). Nothing survives Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the five tests run.

All statistics computed from scratch in pure Python (no scipy): average-rank Spearman, 10,000-draw permutation null, 10,000-resample bootstrap CI, exact Fisher two-sided by hypergeometric enumeration, 10,000-twin permuted negative control. Seed 20260730 (main) / 99 (verification).
hypotheses.code:
import json, math, random
random.seed(20260730)
recs = json.load(open('/home/user/potentially-profitable/data/ingredient-state-record.json'))['records']
panel = [r for r in recs if r.get('import_reliance_pct') is not None
                        and r.get('import_source_hhi') is not None]   # n=72

def mean(v): return sum(v)/len(v)
def pearson(x,y):
    mx,my=mean(x),mean(y)
    sxy=sum((a-mx)*(b-my) for a,b in zip(x,y))
    sxx=sum((a-mx)**2 for a in x); syy=sum((b-my)**2 for b in y)
    return float('nan') if sxx==0 or syy==0 else sxy/math.sqrt(sxx*syy)
def rank(v):                      # average ranks, ties handled
    idx=sorted(range(len(v)),key=lambda i:v[i]); r=[0.0]*len(v); i=0
    while i<len(idx):
        j=i
        while j+1<len(idx) and v[idx[j+1]]==v[idx[i]]: j+=1
        avg=(i+j)/2.0+1.0
        for k in range(i,j+1): r[idx[k]]=avg
        i=j+1
    return r
def spearman(x,y): return pearson(rank(x),rank(y))

def perm_p(x,y,B=10000):          # two-sided permutation null on |rho|
    obs=spearman(x,y); yy=list(y); c=0
    for _ in range(B):
        random.shuffle(yy)
        if abs(spearman(x,yy))>=abs(obs)-1e-15: c+=1
    return obs,(c+1)/(B+1)

def boot_ci(x,y,B=10000,a=0.05):  # bootstrap CI -- the load-bearing stat for a null claim
    m=len(x); out=[]
    for _ in range(B):
        idx=[random.randrange(m) for _ in range(m)]
        s=spearman([x[i] for i in idx],[y[i] for i in idx])
        if not math.isnan(s): out.append(s)
    out.sort(); return out[int(a/2*len(out))], out[int((1-a/2)*len(out))-1]

def run(rows,label):
    x=[r['import_reliance_pct'] for r in rows]; y=[r['import_source_hhi'] for r in rows]
    rho,p=perm_p(x,y); lo,hi=boot_ci(x,y)
    print(f"{label} n={len(rows)}  pearson={pearson(x,y):+.4f}  rho={rho:+.4f}  p={p:.4f}  CI[{lo:+.4f},{hi:+.4f}]")

run(panel,"POOLED")
run([r for r in panel if r['import_reliance_scope']=='item'],     "ITEM ")
run([r for r in panel if r['import_reliance_scope']=='commodity'],"COMM ")

# MANDATORY: commodity-scope rows are NOT independent -- one group number is stamped
# onto every member slug. Collapse to one row per NASS commodity.
from collections import defaultdict
g=defaultdict(list)
for r in panel:
    if r['import_reliance_scope']=='commodity': g[r['nass_commodity']].append(r)
gx=[v[0]['import_reliance_pct'] for v in g.values()]
gy=[mean([q['import_source_hhi'] for q in v]) for v in g.values()]
rho,p=perm_p(gx,gy); print(f"COMMODITY GROUPS COLLAPSED n={len(gx)} rho={rho:+.4f} p={p:.4f}")

# 2x2 joint corner vs the independence expectation
RT,HT=75,0.50; n=len(panel)
a=sum(1 for r in panel if r['import_reliance_pct']>=RT and r['import_source_hhi']>=HT)
nr=sum(1 for r in panel if r['import_reliance_pct']>=RT)
nh=sum(1 for r in panel if r['import_source_hhi']>=HT)
print(f"corner obs={a}  expected under independence={nr*nh/n:.2f}  ratio={a/(nr*nh/n):.2f}")
for r in sorted([x for x in panel if x['import_reliance_pct']>=RT and x['import_source_hhi']>=HT],
                key=lambda r:-r['import_reliance_pct']):
    ts=(r.get('import_top_sources') or [{}])[0]
    print(f"  {r['name']:22s} rel={r['import_reliance_pct']:4d}% hhi={r['import_source_hhi']:.2f} "
          f"{ts.get('country')} {ts.get('share_pct')}%  scope={r['import_reliance_scope']}")
hypotheses.caveats:
SAMPLE SIZE IS SMALL AND THE INDEPENDENT SAMPLE IS SMALLER STILL. n=72 rows, but only 48 are independent observations (37 item-scope + 11 collapsed commodity groups). The high-reliance arm — the one that matters for the corner — is just 20 rows. The pooled CI [-0.157, +0.325] rules out |rho| ≥ 0.33 but CANNOT distinguish true zero from a weak-to-moderate rho of +0.30. This is an orthogonality result at the resolution of "not moderate or strong," not a proof of exact zero.

THE COMMODITY-STAMPING ARTIFACT IS THE HEADLINE HAZARD. 35 of 72 panel rows carry a group-level reliance figure stamped onto every member slug (all five peppers = 82%, all five lettuces = 12%, all four squashes = 48%). Pooling them fakes an n of 35 where the real n is 11. Anyone running this join naively on the commodity subset would report rho = +0.363 with p = 0.031 and conclude the axes DO compound. They do not; the effect vanishes (rho = +0.146, p = 0.67) on collapse. This also means the 13-slug corner is really 8 structural units — the five peppers are one PEPPERS observation and the two tomatoes are one TOMATOES observation.

SELECTION EFFECT — THE PANEL IS ENRICHED FOR CONCENTRATION. Median HHI is 0.590 in the panel (n=72) vs 0.370 in the 81 excluded rows that have HHI but no reliance (53 of those 81 are specialty rows). Reliance requires a NASS domestic-production denominator, which exists mainly for crops the US actually grows commercially. So the panel is not a random or representative slice of the 153 HHI-bearing ingredients, and the 61% "concentrated" base rate is a property of THIS panel, not of the tracked corpus or of US food imports generally. The corner list is likewise conditioned on having a NASS commodity match.

RANGE RESTRICTION. Reliance is heavily right-skewed: q1=12, median=32, q3=80, max=112. Only 20 of 72 rows clear 75%. A correlation computed over a distribution with most mass in the low range has limited leverage to detect a relationship that only exists at the top.

UNITS — BOTH AXES ARE NOMINAL VALUE, NEITHER IS VOLUME OR SUPPLY. import_reliance_pct is a cross-point ratio: customs import value (which carries freight) over (NASS farm-gate production value + imports − exports), year-aligned. It is never a shelf share, never a tonnage share, never a supply-security score, and legitimately exceeds 100 for four rows (re-export), which were not clamped. import_source_hhi is a Herfindahl over import VALUE shares across all source countries. HS6 does not publish quantity, so no volume version of either statistic exists. Both are undeflated nominal USD.

HHI vs TOP-SOURCES ARE NOT RECONCILABLE. import_source_hhi is computed over ALL source countries; import_top_sources is truncated to 3 and its shares do not sum to 100. I used top_sources for corner DISPLAY only and never in any computation, so no statistic here is contaminated by the truncation — but a reader cannot verify the HHI from the printed country list.

CONSTRUCTION CHECK — NOT A TAUTOLOGY, AND NOT FORCED APART EITHER. The reliance denominator includes US domestic production, which the HHI never touches; the HHI is computed only among import sources, which the reliance numerator aggregates over without regard to origin. The two are built from partly disjoint inputs, so there is no definitional mechanism forcing either correlation or independence. That supports the null being a real structural fact rather than an arithmetic consequence — but it also means both inherit the double-counting hazard of the trade layer (16 export values shared across 52 slugs; 7 import code+value pairs shared across 14 slugs), which is why per-slug reliance for code-sharing pairs like lemon/lime is not fully independent either.

MULTIPLICITY. Five correlation tests were run on one panel. Under Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 nothing passes, including the commodity-scope p=0.0314 (threshold 0.0100). The 20-cell threshold sensitivity sweep is another 20 tests; its minimum p was 0.2498, so no correction changes that conclusion. The permuted-twin negative control (10,000 draws) put the observed corner count of 13 at the null mean of 12.23, inside the null 95% range [9,16] — the pipeline does not manufacture a corner from noise.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. It is descriptive of the tracked record on one 2026-07-24 snapshot — a single vintage, no time dimension, no replication on an earlier vintage. It says nothing about whether either axis predicts price movement, volatility, or disruption; no such variable was tested. Independence of two structural descriptors is not evidence that either is or is not a useful risk indicator on its own. Origin shares are a 2025 snapshot not year-aligned to the reliance year (2025 on 70 rows, but 2024/2017/2010 on one each).

THE CLAIM'S "MOSTLY-DIFFERENT SETS" WORDING IS REFUTED, which is why this is scored partial rather than confirmed. 13 of 20 high-reliance ingredients (65%) are also concentrated. The sets overlap heavily. What is true is that the overlap is exactly the base rate (61%), lift 1.06x.

hypotheses.claim: The public record as currently shipped CANNOT determine whether episodes are clustering more over time: the detected-events file caps each ingredient at topN=6 lifetime moves, so recent years are represented only by moves extreme enough to beat 25 years of that ingredient's own history, and after re-detecting without the cap the per-alive-series episode rate and mean cohort size show {R} — with the shipped file the apparent 2024-to-2026 jump in mean cohort size (2.00 to 6.47 on a near-constant panel) {survives / does not survive}.
hypotheses.measuredResult:
DETECTOR FIDELITY FIRST: I copied scripts/build-cost-index-events.mjs and changed exactly 4 lines (repo root, output path, TOP_N from env, export build). At TOP_N=6 my copy reproduces data/cost-index-events.json BYTE-FOR-BYTE (219,759 bytes both). So the uncapped run is the shipped detector with one constant changed, not a re-implementation.

CENSORING (Step 1). 65 of 102 slugs (63.7%) sit exactly at topN=6. Uncapped (TOP_N=Infinity, all other params shipped): 2,634 events vs 432 shipped = 6.10x. Overall survival 16.4%. Those 65 censored slugs actually have 2,592 events; 2,202 (85%) are suppressed. Uncapped events per censored slug: min 6, median 44, max 74. Survival is NOT year-uniform: 7.7% (2016), 9.6% (2023), 15.7% (2024), 26.5% (2025), 27.9% (2026).

COVERAGE KILL CONDITION (falsified only if uncapped reproduces shipped per-year cohort profile within 15% EVERY year): 26 of 26 years exceed 15%. Worst 723.3% (2023: shipped 1.50 vs uncapped 12.35). Smallest 67.6% (2011). NOT FALSIFIED — the coverage claim stands decisively.

R (Step 3). Balanced panel = slugs alive every year 2001-2026 → n=61 (the hypothesis guessed 63; 63 is the 2001 alive count, 61 survive through 2026). 2,466 uncapped events on it (357 shipped). Final spec — uncapped, balanced, edge-trimmed, Poisson with offset log(observed series-weeks), 2001-2025, 2,332 events over 75,771 exposure weeks: year coef -0.00658/yr, rate ratio 0.9934 (-0.66%/yr), quasi-Poisson 95% CI [-0.01180, -0.00136] → RR [0.9883, 0.9986], phi=0.807. Untrimmed 2001-2026: -0.00702 (-0.70%/yr), CI [-0.01193, -0.00212]; negative-binomial -0.00689, CI [-0.01206, -0.00173]. MEAN COHORT SIZE (cohorts recomputed restricted to the balanced panel, n=2,466 events): -0.00711/yr, ratio 0.9929 (-0.71%/yr), quasi 95% CI [-0.00945, -0.00476], phi=2.774. So R = FLAT-TO-SLIGHTLY-DECLINING on both metrics, roughly -0.7%/yr, CIs entirely below zero — the opposite sign from "clustering more."

CLUSTERING (Step 4, 2,000 circular-shift surrogates, balanced panel, 1,306 weekly bins, 2001-04-25..2026-05-01). Observed variance of the weekly active-ingredient count = 21.893; surrogate median 14.188, 5-95% [12.720, 15.713], max 17.693; empirical p = 0.0005. Real cross-ingredient alignment EXISTS and is far outside the surrogate null. But RISING? late-half/early-half variance ratio = 0.9117 vs surrogate median 0.9620, 5-95% [0.7723, 1.1908], p(ratio >= observed) = 0.6537. NO evidence of increasing clustering.

THE JUMP DOES NOT SURVIVE. Shipped: 2024 mean cohort 2.0000 (n=17) → 2026 6.4737 (n=19) = 3.24x, Mann-Whitney p=0.0008. Uncapped: 14.87 (n=108) → 18.35 (n=68) = 1.23x. And the shipped file's FULL-record cohort trend is already negative (-1.14%/yr, 95% CI [-1.92%, -0.38%], n=432) — the "jump" is a local 2023-2026 feature, not a shipped trend.

TWO MECHANISMS, ONE UNANTICIPATED. (a) The shipped per-year mean cohort is largely a restatement of how many events survived the cap that year: Spearman rho = 0.584 (p=0.0017), Pearson r = 0.433 (p=0.027) across 26 year-cells. (b) THE BIGGER ONE, which the hypothesis did not anticipate: ALL 68 uncapped and ALL 19 shipped calendar-2026 events (100%) lie within 26 observations of a series end. Deep history ends 2026-07-01, so the whole of calendar 2026 sits inside the terminal window where the centered ±26-week baseline CANNOT be formed — every 2026 "normal" is one-sided. After edge-trimming, calendar 2026 has ZERO analyzable events. The edge zone is 5.3% of observations but carries 1.14x the event rate. The 6.47 figure — the single number that makes "everything is moving at once now" look true — is computed entirely against truncated baselines and is not comparable to any interior year.
hypotheses.revisedClaim: The shipped detected-events file cannot support any temporal RATE or CLUSTERING claim, for two independent reasons — one documented, one not. (1) The topN=6 cap is severely binding: 65 of 102 slugs (63.7%) sit exactly at it, only 16.4% of real episodes survive (432 of 2,634), and survival is not year-uniform (7.7% in 2016 vs 27.9% in 2026), so the shipped per-year cohort profile is largely a restatement of censoring density (Spearman rho=0.584, p=0.0017) and misses the uncapped profile by 15%+ in 26 of 26 years, worst 723%. (2) UNDOCUMENTED: because the deep history ends 2026-07-01 and the baseline is a centered ±26-week median, 100% of calendar-2026 events (68 uncapped, 19 shipped) fall inside the terminal window where that baseline is one-sided — after edge-trimming, 2026 has zero analyzable events. The apparent 2024→2026 cohort jump (2.00 → 6.47, 3.24x) DOES NOT SURVIVE: it shrinks to 1.23x uncapped (14.87 → 18.35), the panel it sits on grew 16% (86 → 102 → 100 slugs, not "near-constant"), and its 2026 endpoint is entirely edge-artifact. Re-detected without the cap on a balanced 61-slug panel alive every year 2001-2026, both metrics run flat-to-slightly-DOWN, not up: episode rate -0.66%/yr (RR 0.9934, 95% CI [0.9883, 0.9986]) and mean cohort size -0.71%/yr (ratio 0.9929, 95% CI [0.9906, 0.9952]). Episodes DO co-occur far more than chance (weekly active-count variance 21.893 vs surrogate median 14.188, p=0.0005 on 2,000 circular shifts) — but that alignment is not increasing (late/early variance ratio 0.9117, p=0.65). ## 1. Faithful parameterization (NOT a re-implementation)
cp scripts/build-cost-index-events.mjs detector.mjs   # then 4 line edits:
#   const repo = '/home/user/potentially-profitable';                  (was path.resolve(__dirname,'..'))
#   const OUT  = '<scratchpad>/out-events.json';                       (never write into the repo)
#   const TOP_N = process.env.TOP_N==='inf' ? Infinity : (+process.env.TOP_N||6);
#   export { build };  if (process.env.RUN_MAIN==='1') main();
# FIDELITY GATE — must pass before trusting anything:
#   JSON.stringify(build(),null,2)+'\n' === readFileSync('data/cost-index-events.json')  -> true (219,759 bytes)

## 2. Censoring + per-year profile
sat = sum(1 for v in shipped['items'].values() if v['eventCount']==6)          # 65 / 102
for y in 2001..2026: survival[y] = shipped_events[y] / uncapped_events[y]      # 7.7% .. 27.9%
# coverage kill condition: |mean_cohort_unc[y] - mean_cohort_ship[y]| / mean_cohort_ship[y] <= 0.15 for ALL y

## 3. Balanced panel + Poisson GLM (IRLS by hand; statsmodels unavailable)
BAL = [k for k,(first,last) in spanYear.items() if first<=2001 and last>=2026]  # n=61
expo[y] = sum of observed series-weeks in year y over BAL, EXCLUDING the first/last 26 obs of each series
cnt[y]  = uncapped events on BAL in year y, same edge trim
X = [1, year-mean(year)];  offset = log(expo)
def poisson_glm(y,X,offset):            # IRLS: eta=Xb+off; mu=exp(eta); W=mu; z=eta-off+(y-mu)/mu
    b = solve(X'WX, X'Wz) until converged
    cov = inv(X' diag(mu) X);  phi = sum((y-mu)^2/mu)/df;  se_quasi = sqrt(diag(cov))*sqrt(phi)
# -> beta_year = -0.00658, quasi 95% CI [-0.01180, -0.00136], phi=0.807
# NB cross-check via scipy.optimize on nbinom loglik -> -0.00689, CI [-0.01206,-0.00173]

## 4. Circular-shift surrogates (clustering)
for k in BAL: active[k] = boolean over that slug's own observation index, True on [iLo..iHi] of each episode
weekly[w] = # of BAL slugs active in global week w   (w = (date - t0)//7, 1306 bins)
stat = var(weekly)                                            # observed 21.893
for b in 1..2000:  shift each slug's active vector by np.roll(active, U{0..n-1})  # preserves that slug's
    surrogate[b] = var(weekly_from_shifted)                   # episode count, durations, internal spacing
p = (1 + #{surrogate >= stat}) / 2001                         # 0.0005
# rising-clustering: ratio = var(weekly[half:]) / var(weekly[:half]) = 0.9117, surrogate p = 0.6537

## 5. Edge artifact (the unanticipated finding)
edge = [e for e in events if e.iPk < 26 or e.iPk >= len(series)-26]
# calendar-2026: 68 of 68 uncapped, 19 of 19 shipped, are in `edge` -> 100%
hypotheses.caveats:
SMALL n WHERE IT MATTERS, LOUDLY: the annual regression has only 25-26 YEAR CELLS. It aggregates 2,332 events, but the trend is fitted on 25 points, so the tight-looking CI on the year coefficient rests on a short series. The effect is also economically trivial (-0.66%/yr compounds to about -15% over 25 years) — I would not publish it as "episodes are becoming rarer"; the honest read is "flat, with no detectable rise."

MECHANICAL NON-COMPARABILITY OF COHORT SIZE ACROSS RUNS: cohort size counts other events within ±6 weeks, so it scales with total event count. Uncapped cohorts (mean ~15) are mechanically larger than shipped (mean ~4) and the ABSOLUTE values are not comparable between runs. Only the temporal PROFILE within a run is interpretable — which is exactly the comparison I made. For the balanced-panel cohort regression I recomputed cohorts restricted to the 61 panel members precisely to remove the panel-growth inflation.

SURROGATE CAVEAT: a uniform random circular shift preserves each ingredient's episode count, durations and internal spacing, but does NOT preserve calendar-month position. So the p=0.0005 alignment result may partly reflect shared seasonality (many produce items peak in the same months) rather than episode-specific co-movement. The testSpec asserted seasonal position is preserved; it is not. The RISING test (late/early variance ratio, p=0.65) is unaffected by this because both halves share the same seasonal structure.

SURVIVORSHIP: the balanced panel (61 of 102) is by construction the long-lived series — mostly AMS terminal-market produce with 25-year histories. It excludes every recently-added slug and all 16 seafood items with no deep series. The flat rate is a statement about long-tracked ingredients, not about the current 100-ingredient panel.

DEFINITIONAL: "episode" here is entirely the shipped detector's construct — a >=20% sustained departure from a centered ±26-week own-series median on a 3-week-smoothed nominal series. A different floor or window would give different counts. Values are nominal cents per each ingredient's own trading unit with NO inflation adjustment across 25 years, and no unit field exists in this file; I never compared levels across ingredients, only within-series deviations, so the unit trap does not bite here. pctFromNormal is a whole integer percent in this file (not a fraction) — handled.

EDGE FINDING IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATISTICAL: the claim that 100% of calendar-2026 events sit in the one-sided-baseline zone is arithmetic, not inference — history ends 2026-07-01 and 26 weekly observations back is roughly 2025-12-31. It is guaranteed by construction, which is precisely why it is a real and permanent defect for the most recent year on every rebuild, not a one-off.

PREMISE ERROR IN THE HYPOTHESIS, CORRECTED: "on a near-constant panel" is FALSE. The alive panel runs 75 (2023) → 86 (2024) → 102 (2025) → 100 (2026), a 16% rise across the window in question. Panel growth is part of the explanation, not excluded from it. Also the balanced panel is 61, not the 63 the hypothesis assumed (63 is the 2001 alive count).

NOT TESTED: I did not attempt any causal or mechanistic account of why alignment exists, and the alignment result is co-occurrence only. co-movement.json was inspected but not analyzed; it is derived from the capped file and inherits every truncation reported here.

import json, os
ROOT = "/home/user/potentially-profitable"
L = lambda p: json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, p)))

mp   = {r["slug"]: r for r in L("cost-index/menu-pricing.json")["ingredients"]}
seas = {r["slug"]: r for r in L("cost-index/seasonality.json")["ingredients"]}
dep  = L("data/ingredient-depth.json")["ingredients"]
lf   = L("data/cost-lockfloat.json")["items"]

panel = [s for s, r in mp.items() if r.get("cheapest_month") is not None]   # 54

surv, fail_store, no_store, fail_band = [], [], [], []
for s in sorted(panel):
    cheap  = mp[s]["cheapest_month"]                 # GATED trough (noise-tested)
    pricey = seas[s]["priciest_month"]               # naive peak
    gap    = ((pricey - cheap) + 12) % 12            # months trough -> peak

    d  = dep.get(s, {})
    fz = d.get("freezeMonths"); sl = d.get("shelfLifeDays")
    hold       = fz if fz is not None else (sl/30 if sl is not None else None)
    hold_fresh = sl/30 if sl is not None else None   # strict variant: no freezing

    save, band = mp[s]["save_pct"], mp[s]["band_pct"]   # both PERCENTS
    if band is None:                                   # split via lockfloat reason
        r = lf[s].get("reason")
        gateB = {"no-series": None, "flat": True, "volatile": False}.get(r)
    else:
        gateB = save > band

    if hold is None:      no_store.append(s)
    elif hold < gap:      fail_store.append(s)
    elif gateB is False:  fail_band.append(s)
    elif gateB is True:   surv.append((s, cheap, pricey, gap, fz, sl, save, band))

print("N =", len(surv), "of", len(panel))
print("fails-storage", len(fail_store), "no-storage-data", len(no_store),
      "fails-band", len(fail_band))

# --- the decisive sensitivity: same gates, but freezing not allowed ---
strict = [s for s in panel
          if (dep.get(s, {}).get("shelfLifeDays") or 0)/30
             >= ((seas[s]["priciest_month"] - mp[s]["cheapest_month"]) + 12) % 12
          and mp[s]["save_pct"] > mp[s]["band_pct"]]
print("N with fresh shelf life only =", len(strict))   # -> 0

# --- independent bite of each gate over all 54 (not sequential) ---
print("band gate alone fails:",
      [s for s in panel if mp[s]["save_pct"] <= mp[s]["band_pct"]])   # -> 3

# --- consistency: does save_pct use the same month pair as the gap? ---
ok = sum(1 for s in panel
         if abs(round((seas[s]["months"][f"{seas[s]['priciest_month']:02d}"]["median_cents"]
                     - seas[s]["months"][f"{mp[s]['cheapest_month']:02d}"]["median_cents"])
                    / seas[s]["months"][f"{seas[s]['priciest_month']:02d}"]["median_cents"] * 100)
                - mp[s]["save_pct"]) <= 1)
print("save_pct reproduced from the same month pair:", ok, "/", len(panel))  # 54/54
hypotheses.caveats:
SAMPLE SIZE IS SMALL AND PRE-FILTERED. n = 54, and every named bucket is single digits to low twenties. The 54 are not a random sample of the 100-ingredient catalog: they are the rows that (a) had a "ready" seasonal baseline (84 of 100) and (b) cleared menu-pricing's dispersion robustness test AND a >=15% saving floor. So the panel is deliberately pre-selected for large, robust seasonal swings. Any share quoted here is a share of that filtered set, never of the catalog.

THE BAND GATE IS PARTLY TAUTOLOGICAL. save_pct only exists when it already exceeds 15 (TIMING_MIN_SAVE in scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs), and the median band_pct is 12.6. The test "is the saving bigger than the band" is therefore asking a question the upstream builder has largely already answered. Its 3-of-54 bite is close to the floor you would expect from that construction alone — I did not treat it as an independent test and neither should any published version.

THE STORAGE GATE COLLAPSES TO A FREEZE-AVAILABILITY LOOKUP. 28 of 54 clear it and all 28 have a freezeMonths figure; 0 of the 17 panel rows lacking freezeMonths clear it on shelf life. For 11 of the 26 survivors freezeMonths >= 12, which exceeds the maximum possible gap (11), so gate A is vacuous on those rows. The gate is closer to "did the depth researchers record a freeze life for this item" than to a measured carrying test.

FREEZING IS NOT A NEUTRAL HOLD. The spec's holdMonths rule treats a 12-month freeze life as equivalent capacity to holding fresh. Operationally it is not: frozen blueberries work in a coulis, frozen brussels sprouts and asparagus are a different product than fresh, and the 26-item list is a freeze-and-hold list, not a fresh-buy list. Any published version must say "buy in month M and freeze" and must not imply the item is available fresh at the peak. It also silently assumes freezer capacity, labor to process at the trough, and no carrying cost — none of which are in any of these files.

HORIZON MISMATCH ON THE BAND. band_pct is a NEXT-WEEK conformal reach, used here as a noise floor for a multi-month hold. It understates multi-month drift, so gate B is if anything too lenient — conservative in the direction of admitting items, not excluding them. The result "only 2 fail on band" is therefore an upper bound on how permissive the panel is, not a demonstration that seasonal savings comfortably beat noise over a season.

STORAGE FIGURES ARE BOOK VALUES, NOT OBSERVATIONS. freezeMonths and shelfLifeDays come from ingredient-depth.json, which is sourced from reference/extension material with per-row confidence labels, not from Don's kitchen. shelfLifeDays is explicitly the CUT/prepped life; several items keep far longer whole (acorn squash: shelfLifeDays 5 for cut pieces, 1-2 months whole per its storageMethod prose). Using the cut figure makes the fresh-only variant harsher than reality for whole-stored items — which is exactly why the fresh-only N=0 should be read as "the public record does not support a fresh hold," not as a proven physical impossibility.

DEFINITIONAL MIXING OF TWO cheapest_month RULES. The trough is the noise-gated value from menu-pricing; the peak is seasonality's NAIVE argmax with no robustness test. The peak side is therefore weaker evidence than the trough side. I verified the published save_pct reproduces from exactly this month pair on 54/54, so the two files are internally consistent here, but the asymmetry in rigor between the two endpoints is real.

NOT CAUSAL, NOT A FORECAST, NOT A DELIVERED PRICE. Every cents figure underneath these percentages is a nominal public wholesale reference against each ingredient's own 5-year trailing baseline, in its own trading unit (carton/lb/sack/dozen), undeflated. Nothing here says prices will fall in month M; it says the tracked record's median in month M sat below the median in month N. save_pct and band_pct are both percentages of an item's own baseline and are never cross-comparable in dollars.

ONE ODD SURVIVOR. blueberry carries posture='withhold' (lockfloat reason 'volatile', band 30.1%) — the instrument declines to publish a price read on it, yet it clears both gates because its 57% saving is large. Publishing it on a "buyable" list while the same site withholds its posture would be an internal contradiction that needs an explicit editorial resolution.

But the aggregate excess is NOT robust and the "higher-value half" framing does not survive its own pre-registered fragility test: dropping the single largest dark code — HS 0201305085+0202305085, a NESOI ("not elsewhere specified") residual boneless-beef line that the repo's own crosswalk assigns wholly to ground-beef, worth $5.34B — flips the ratio to 0.898, and trimming the top three codes from both sides flips it to 0.966. The rank test on per-code values is null (Mann-Whitney one-sided p=0.209). The defensible claim is therefore "the dark set is at least comparable in trade value to the published set, on 41% fewer ingredients," not "the record goes dark on the higher-value half." The honest mechanism is narrower still: 70% of the dark trade value comes from the 16 'no-series' withholds and 48% comes from seafood and shellfish alone — categories with no USDA AMS terminal-market wholesale reporting at all. The blind spot is real and large, but it is shaped like "seafood and manufacturing beef trim are import-heavy and have no public wholesale series," not like a value-neutral coverage failure.

hypotheses.caveats:
FALSIFIED AS PRE-REGISTERED. Kill condition K2 ("the ratio falls below 1.0 after dropping the single largest DARK HS6 code — the effect is one-code fragile") fires exactly: 1.1522 → 0.8981. K1 and K3 do not fire. I am reporting "partial" rather than "refuted" because the magnitudes ($24.21B dark vs $21.01B published, and 2× the value per withheld slug) do refute the "small, obscure items" framing the hypothesis set out to attack, while the specific "higher-value half" claim dies on its own robustness test.

THE EFFECT IS DRIVEN BY A RESIDUAL CODE, AND THAT IS A MODELING CHOICE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The single code that decides the outcome is HS 0201305085+0202305085, sdesc "MEAT,BVNE BNELESS FR/CH US NT 3 EXC PRCSD,NESOI" — NESOI means "not elsewhere specified or indicated," i.e. an explicit catch-all bucket. data/ingredient-hs-codes.json's own note calls it "boneless beef not in a named primal — the lean manufacturing trim that feeds grinding," and assigns 100% of it to the slug `ground-beef`. If that residual line were apportioned across the beef primals (ribeye, striploin, tenderloin are all `lock`), or excluded as unallocable, the entire aggregate excess disappears. The finding rests on an authored crosswalk decision.

VALUE, NOT VOLUME, NOT SUPPLY. us_import_value_usd is nominal US customs general-import value, undeflated, annual. HS6 publishes no quantity, so this figure mixes price and volume and cannot be read as tonnage, supply, or availability. A commodity whose price rose contributes more "trade value" without a single extra pound crossing a port.

LIKELY PARTIAL TAUTOLOGY / SURVIVORSHIP. 70.1% of the dark trade value comes from the 16 'no-series' withholds, and 48.0% comes from seafood + shellfish (13 codes, $11.63B). "No public wholesale series" for those slugs is not a coincidence with import value — the Muntin price spine is built on USDA AMS terminal markets and USDA LMR, which do not cover seafood at all, while seafood is simultaneously one of the most import-dependent food categories in the US. So a large part of what looks like "the record goes dark where the money is" is really "the record is a produce-and-livestock instrument, and seafood is both outside it and imported." That is still a genuine, publishable coverage gap, but the causal-sounding version of the claim is close to definitional.

n IS SMALL AND THE DISTRIBUTION IS SEVERELY SKEWED. 30 vs 50 code-level observations. The top 3 dark codes are 47.5% of the dark sum. Any sum comparison over 30 heavy-tailed draws is fragile by construction — the jackknife result is a property of the sample size and skew as much as of the phenomenon.

THE INFERENCE IS AMBIGUOUS AND THE p-VALUES ARE UNCORRECTED AND POST-HOC. The permutation test on the sum ratio gives p=0.0464, but the median ratio gives p=0.2559 and Mann-Whitney U — the test that actually asks whether dark codes are systematically larger — gives one-sided p=0.2090, not significant. The sum-based statistic is the one the tail drives. I ran multiple statistics after seeing the data and applied no multiplicity correction; treat none of these p-values as gating.

ONE CODE STRADDLES THE BOUNDARY. HS 080550 is carried by lime (withhold) and lemon (lock), so its ~$972M is counted once in each group under the spec's method. Excluding it from both moves the ratio only from 1.1522 to 1.1596 — immaterial.

DERIVED-CLASSIFIER DEPENDENCE. `bucket` is entirely Muntin-derived (a conformal band width plus a Wilson-CI coverage floor over its own deep history), not an external standard. The dark/published partition is this instrument's own editorial threshold, so the finding describes where THIS instrument declines to publish, not a property of the public record in general.

NOT A DELIVERED PRICE AND NOT A CAUSAL CLAIM. Nothing here touches what any operator pays, and the co-occurrence of "high import value" with "withheld" is association only.
