hypotheses.caveats:
SAMPLE SIZES ARE SMALL AND MUST BE STATED LOUDLY. The magnitude statistic rests on n=36. The sign test rests on n=46 and its confidence strata are n=12/27/7 — the "high confidence" stratum is 12 rows, which can detect essentially nothing. The category strata run n=1 to n=11; the shellfish result (1 vs 7, p=0.0703) is one of 9 strata tested, is uncorrected, and would not survive Benjamini-Hochberg at any q. Do not report it as a seafood bias.

THE BIGGEST THREAT IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT STATISTICAL. At least 10 of the 36 priced disagreements (and 13 of 46 overall) are not two tables disagreeing about the same quantity — the depth row's own prose names the manifest's number as a different cut, prep state, or species. This is a conservative lower bound from a crude 0.02-window regex over cutSpec/yieldNote/yieldSource; spinach misses the window by 0.01 and is plainly the same case. So "the tables disagree" overstates it; "the tables pin different, undeclared specifications and the published one carries no spec field" is what the data supports. Two of the three largest magnitudes are exactly this: whole-crab is blue crab (0.17) vs Dungeness/king (0.25-0.27), and octopus is cleaned-only (0.80, with the depth row explicitly recording "Cook yield rejected") vs a manifest 0.45 that appears to bake in braise loss. Publishing "47% cost swing" without that caveat would itself be the fabrication.

DELTA_PCT DENOMINATOR IS ASYMMETRIC by construction — I divided by the manifest epCents because the manifest is the published number, so the figure reads as "how far off the published value could be." Recomputing against the depth denominator gives median 7.7% but max 77.7% (octopus). The choice changes the headline max by 30pp. Both are stated.

SURVIVORSHIP / SELECTION. The 36 priced rows are not a random sample of the 46 disagreements: 8 of the 10 excluded slugs are absent from cost-index.json entirely and 3 more have a null level — and those are disproportionately seafood and specialty produce, exactly where yield tables diverge most. The magnitude statistic is therefore conditioned on "has a public wholesale reference," which is itself the instrument's own coverage filter.

UNITS. Every cents figure is nominal US cents per that ingredient's own trading unit (25 of the 36 are cartons, 11 are lb), taken from cost-index-labels.json. No per-pound normalization exists anywhere in the repo, so cross-ingredient cents comparison is meaningless and none is made. These are public wholesale reference levels, never delivered or invoice price. Level asOf spans 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-24 (5 rows are 12 weeks stale), so this is a snapshot, not a series.

CITRUS. Exactly 1 of the 36 (lemon, 7.1%) is a citrus row where the manifest `yield` is JUICE yield, so its trim tax is a juice-extraction cost, not knife trim. Excluding it does not move the result (n=35, median 7.6%, max 47.1%). Lime/orange/grapefruit are not in the priced disagreement set (orange disagrees but has no live level; lime and grapefruit agree within 0.005).

NEITHER TABLE IS AN OBSERVATION. Both are book/reference values — the manifest's 113 rows are drift-gated against the CIA YIELD_TABLE in tools/plate-cost/plate-cost.js with 5 cited to USDA FBG; the depth rows cite US Foods Common Product Yields, USDA FoodData Central, NCHFP and extension services. Nothing here came from anyone's kitchen and nothing here establishes which table is correct — that question is not answerable from this repo.

NOT A TAUTOLOGY, AND THE SILENT-USE AUDIT IS CLEAN. epCents = level / yield is definitional, but the 84/84-vs-0/84 split is a real provenance finding, not circular: it establishes that the depth table has zero influence on any published figure. The one apparent mismatch (bok-choy) was a Python banker's-rounding artifact in my first pass and disappears under JS Math.round; I re-ran and report the corrected 84/84.

PRIOR ART. USDA ERS Fruit and Vegetable Prices already joins edible-yield factors to price, but at retail (Circana scanner, latest pricing 2022), annually, for household cost-per-serving, using a single yield source. The table-vs-table disagreement at wholesale is the extension. Nothing here is a first-ever.

hypotheses.caveats:
SAMPLE SIZES ARE SMALL AND MUST BE STATED LOUDLY. The magnitude statistic rests on n=36. The sign test rests on n=46 and its confidence strata are n=12/27/7 — the "high confidence" stratum is 12 rows and can detect essentially nothing. The category strata run n=1 to n=11; the shellfish result (1 vs 7, p=0.0703) is one of 9 strata tested, is uncorrected, and survives no Benjamini-Hochberg correction at any q. Do not report it as a seafood bias.

THE BIGGEST THREAT IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT STATISTICAL. At least 10 of the 36 priced disagreements (13 of 46 overall) are not two tables disagreeing about the same quantity — the depth row's own prose names the manifest's number as a different cut, prep state, or species. This is a conservative lower bound from a crude 0.02-window regex over cutSpec/yieldNote/yieldSource; spinach misses the window by 0.01 and is plainly the same case. So "the tables disagree" overstates it; "the tables pin different, undeclared specifications, and the published one carries no spec field" is what the data supports. Two of the three largest magnitudes are exactly this: whole-crab is blue crab (0.17) vs Dungeness/king (0.25-0.27), and octopus is cleaned-only (0.80, with the depth row explicitly recording "Cook yield rejected") against a manifest 0.45 that appears to bake in braise loss. Publishing "47% cost swing" without that caveat would itself be the fabrication.

DELTA_PCT DENOMINATOR IS ASYMMETRIC by construction — I divided by the manifest epCents because the manifest is the published number, so the figure reads as "how far off the published value could be." Recomputing against the depth denominator gives median 7.7% but max 77.7% (octopus). The choice changes the headline max by 30pp. Both are stated.

SURVIVORSHIP / SELECTION. The 36 priced rows are not a random sample of the 46 disagreements: 7 of the 10 excluded slugs are absent from cost-index.json entirely and 3 more have a null level — and those skew seafood and specialty produce, exactly where yield tables diverge most. The magnitude statistic is conditioned on "has a public wholesale reference," which is the instrument's own coverage filter.

UNITS. Every cents figure is nominal US cents per that ingredient's own trading unit (25 of the 36 are cartons, 11 are lb), taken from cost-index-labels.json. No per-pound normalization exists anywhere in the repo, so cross-ingredient cents comparison is meaningless and none is made. These are public wholesale reference levels, never delivered or invoice price. Level asOf spans 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-24 (5 rows are 12 weeks stale), so this is a snapshot, not a series.

CITRUS. Exactly 1 of the 36 (lemon, 7.1%) is a citrus row where the manifest `yield` is JUICE yield, so its trim tax is a juice-extraction cost, not knife trim. Excluding it does not move the result (n=35, median 7.6%, max 47.1%). Lime/orange/grapefruit are not in the priced disagreement set: orange disagrees but has no live level; lime and grapefruit agree within 0.005.

NEITHER TABLE IS AN OBSERVATION, AND NEITHER IS SHOWN CORRECT. Both are book/reference values — the manifest's 113 rows are drift-gated against the CIA YIELD_TABLE in tools/plate-cost/plate-cost.js with 5 cited to USDA FBG; the depth rows cite US Foods Common Product Yields, USDA FoodData Central, NCHFP and extension services. Nothing here came from anyone's kitchen, and which table is right is not answerable from this repo.

NOT A TAUTOLOGY, AND THE SILENT-USE AUDIT IS CLEAN. epCents = level / yield is definitional, but the 84/84-vs-0/84 split is a real provenance result, not circular: it establishes the depth table has zero influence on any published figure. The one apparent mismatch (bok-choy) was a Python banker's-rounding artifact in my first pass and disappears under JS Math.round; I re-ran and report the corrected 84/84.

PRIOR ART. USDA ERS Fruit and Vegetable Prices already joins edible-yield factors to price, but at retail (Circana scanner, latest pricing 2022), annually, for household cost-per-serving, using a single yield source. The table-vs-table disagreement at wholesale is the extension. Nothing here is a first-ever, and it should not be framed as one.

short=[s for s in slugs if len(deep.get(s,[]))<=10]             # 16; next-shortest is 65
print(sum(1 for s in short if vec(s)[0]==0==vec(s)[1]==vec(s)[4]))  # 16

# SECONDARY: pairwise phi + BH q=0.10 -> only BAND/SEASON/EVENTS pairs survive
def phi(a,b):
    n11=((a==1)&(b==1)).sum(); n10=((a==1)&(b==0)).sum()
    n01=((a==0)&(b==1)).sum(); n00=((a==0)&(b==0)).sum()
    d=((n11+n10)*(n01+n00)*(n11+n01)*(n10+n00))**.5
    return (n11*n00-n10*n01)/d if d>0 else float("nan")
# SEASON~EVENTS +0.8218, BAND~EVENTS +0.6930, BAND~SEASON +0.5695 (all p=5e-5)
# every YIELD pair |phi| <= 0.1084, all n.s.; every TRADE pair |phi| <= 0.1761, all n.s.
hypotheses.caveats:
1. DEFINITIONAL TAUTOLOGY — the dominant caveat, and the reason this is "partial" not "confirmed." The claim's premise of "five independent layers" is false. Three of them (BAND, SEASON, EVENTS) are all computed from data/cost-index-history.json. The proof is structural, not statistical: the missing sets are perfectly nested (missing SEASON ⊂ missing EVENTS ⊂ missing BAND), and 16/16 ingredients with ≤10 deep observations fail all three at once. The pre-registered permutation null asks "could these five vectors have been aligned by chance?" — for three of the five the answer is mechanically no, so the null is a strawman for the exact structure it is being asked to reject. The honest recomputation (collapse the three, test on 3 layers) falsifies at p=0.567.

2. SURVIVORSHIP / INSTRUMENT-CONSTRUCTION EFFECT. The 16-slug core of the dark set is not a fact about seafood markets; it is a fact about which agency covers what. Seafood is not on the AMS terminal-market circuit, so those 15 slugs carry only NOAA's monthly series (9–10 points, all beginning 2025-02-01 — i.e. the instrument only started ingesting them recently). "Dark" here partly means "recently added to this panel," not "unknowable." A rebuild in 18 months could move most of these out of the dark set with no change in the underlying market.

3. THE 5-HERB RESIDUAL IS SMALL AND SITS ON THE PRE-STATED FLOOR. Once the 16 no-series slugs are removed, D drops to 5 of 84 (still p=0.0002 vs a null 95th of 2). D=5 is exactly the testSpec's own "falsified if D < 5" boundary — one ingredient's worth of slack. Any threshold change flips it.

4. THE PUBLISHED "24 of 100 with all four layers" IS NOT WHAT I MEASURED. I scored five layers, got 52/100 at all five and 76/100 at ≥4. Different layer definitions; do not reconcile these two numbers without checking the study's own layer list.

5. p IS FLOOR-LIMITED, NOT EXACT. 0 of 10,000 permutations reached D=21, so the reported p=0.0001/0.0002 is the resolution limit of the iteration count, not a measured tail. Given how far D=21 sits above the null max of 11, the true p is far smaller — but it is also, per caveat 1, the p-value of a question whose premise does not hold.

6. NO MULTIPLICITY CORRECTION ON THE PRIMARY TEST. The primary D test is a single pre-registered statistic, so none is needed there. The 10 pairwise phi tests carry BH at q=0.10 as specified. But the drop-one-layer sweep (5 tests), the collapsed-layer variants (2), the stratified null (1) and the exclude-16 subset (1) were run post hoc as artifact probes and are uncorrected; treat their p-values as diagnostics, not as findings.

7. NO UNITS OR VALUE/VOLUME EXPOSURE. Every quantity here is a binary presence flag or a count of flags; no price, cents, percent, unit-value or trade-value figure enters the statistic, so the carton-vs-lb and value-vs-volume traps do not apply. The one place trade data is touched is a null-check on us_import_value_usd, never its magnitude.

8. HONESTY CONTRACT. A missing layer is a fact about what the public record publishes and about this instrument's willingness to stand behind a read — not a statement about the ingredient, its market, or its stability. The layer count is not a quality score, and the herbs' flat print is a fact about an administered wholesale quote, not evidence that herb prices do not move.

Permutation p = 0.0001 (B = 10,000, two-sided on |rho|). Bootstrap 95% CI = [0.3111, 0.6872] (B = 2,000). Pearson = 0.4603 for context. halfWidthPct range 0.0060-0.2640; amplitude range 0.0600-1.1146.

But the association is almost entirely BETWEEN buckets, and buckets are defined by half-width thresholds. Within-bucket Spearman: lock (n=37) rho = +0.3030, p = 0.0699; cushion (n=19) rho = -0.0772, p = 0.7453; float (n=7) rho = -0.1071, p = 0.8410.

Whole turkey holds a 0.8% next-week band and moves 40.6% across the year; red potato 0.8% and 30.5%; banana 0.6% and 11.8%. 'Lock' is a correct statement about next week and a misleading one about the calendar. hypotheses.code:
import json, math, random, statistics as st
random.seed(20260730)
ROOT = "/home/user/potentially-profitable"
items = json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/data/cost-lockfloat.json"))["items"]
seas  = {r["key"]: r for r in json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/data/seasonality.json"))["ingredients"]}

panel = []
for slug, it in items.items():
    s = seas[slug]
    if not s["ready"] or len(s["months"]) != 12 or it.get("halfWidthPct") is None: continue
    ks = sorted(s["months"], key=int)                      # zero-pad hoisting trap
    med = [s["months"][k]["medianCents"] for k in ks]
    p25 = [s["months"][k]["p25Cents"]    for k in ks]
    p75 = [s["months"][k]["p75Cents"]    for k in ks]
    lo, hi = med.index(min(med)), med.index(max(med))
    panel.append(dict(slug=slug, bucket=it["bucket"], hw=it["halfWidthPct"],
        amp_a=(max(med)-min(med))/st.median(med),          # within-ingredient ratio => unit-safe
        amp_b=(max(med)-min(med))/min(med),
        amp_c=(p75[hi]-p25[lo])/st.median(med),
        min_years=min(s["months"][k]["years"] for k in ks)))

def ranks(xs):                                             # average ranks, ties handled
    o = sorted(range(len(xs)), key=lambda i: xs[i]); r = [0.0]*len(xs); i = 0
    while i < len(o):
        j = i
        while j+1 < len(o) and xs[o[j+1]] == xs[o[i]]: j += 1
        for k in range(i, j+1): r[o[k]] = (i+j)/2.0 + 1.0
        i = j+1
    return r
def pearson(a,b):
    n=len(a); ma=sum(a)/n; mb=sum(b)/n
    return (sum((x-ma)*(y-mb) for x,y in zip(a,b)) /
            (math.sqrt(sum((x-ma)**2 for x in a))*math.sqrt(sum((y-mb)**2 for y in b))))
def spearman(a,b): return pearson(ranks(a), ranks(b))
def perm_p(a,b,B=10000):                                   # two-sided on |rho|
    obs = spearman(a,b); bb = list(b); c = 0
    for _ in range(B):
        random.shuffle(bb)
        if abs(spearman(a,bb)) >= abs(obs)-1e-12: c += 1
    return obs, (c+1)/(B+1)
def boot_ci(a,b,B=2000):
    n=len(a); out=[]
    for _ in range(B):
        idx=[random.randrange(n) for _ in range(n)]
        out.append(spearman([a[i] for i in idx],[b[i] for i in idx]))
    out.sort(); return out[int(.025*B)], out[int(.975*B)]

banded = [p for p in panel if p["bucket"] != "withhold"]
rho, p = perm_p([q["hw"] for q in banded], [q["amp_a"] for q in banded])
print("PRIMARY n=%d rho=%.4f p=%.4f CI=%s" % (len(banded), rho, p,
      boot_ci([q["hw"] for q in banded],[q["amp_a"] for q in banded])))

locks = [q for q in panel if q["bucket"] == "lock"]
L = sum(1 for q in locks if q["amp_a"] > 3*q["hw"])
print("LOCK n=%d  L=%d  median ratio=%.3f" % (len(locks), L,
      st.median([q["amp_a"]/q["hw"] for q in locks])))

for b in ("lock","cushion","float","withhold"):            # secondary 1
    g = [q["amp_a"] for q in panel if q["bucket"] == b]
    print(" %-9s n=%2d median amp=%.4f" % (b, len(g), st.median(g)))
for b in ("lock","cushion","float"):                       # is it only between-bucket?
    g = [q for q in panel if q["bucket"] == b]
    print(" within-%s rho=%+.4f p=%.4f" % (b, *perm_p([q["hw"] for q in g],[q["amp_a"] for q in g])))
# Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney, and the 4-spec sweep run the same permutation machinery.
hypotheses.caveats:
1. SHARED-INPUT EFFECT — the most important caveat. Both statistics are aggregations of the SAME underlying series (data/cost-index-history.json). A noisier price history mechanically produces both a wider next-week conformal band and a wider spread of month-of-year medians. A positive rho is therefore partly expected by construction and is NOT evidence that the lock/float classifier has smuggled in seasonal information. The honest reading of rho = 0.52 is "two different summaries of one volatility profile share about a quarter of their rank variance," not "band width measures season."

2. THE BUCKET ORDERING IS THE PRIMARY CORRELATION RE-BINNED, NOT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE. Buckets are assigned by half-width thresholds (lock <= 0.08, cushion <= 0.20, float <= 0.30), so "median amplitude rises lock -> cushion -> float" is the same fact as the primary rho, coarsened. Within-bucket rhos (lock +0.30 p=0.07, cushion -0.08, float -0.11) are the non-circular version, and they are weak to absent. Secondary 1 should not be counted as confirmation of the primary.

3. AMPLITUDE IS NOT PURELY SEASONAL. It is the spread of month-of-year medians computed over a 5-year trailing window anchored to each series' own latest print, in nominal undeflated cents. Any 5-year level trend or step is absorbed into "amplitude." russet-potato's 111.5% figure is almost certainly not a clean annual cycle. This inflates amplitude for trending items and therefore inflates both rho and L to an unquantified degree. A trend/season decomposition would be needed to separate them and was not performed.

4. RHO CROSSES THE KILL LINE BY 0.019 AND THE CI STRADDLES IT. The bootstrap 95% CI is [0.31, 0.69]. "rho >= 0.5" is not a robust conclusion — it is a point estimate landing just past a pre-registered threshold. I am reporting it as falsified because that is what the pre-registration said, not because the data cleanly separates 0.52 from 0.45.

5. SURVIVORSHIP. 18 of 100 catalog slugs are excluded for lacking a ready 12-month seasonal baseline, and the seasonality gate itself requires >=2 distinct years per month and >=6 established months — so the panel is biased toward ingredients with longer, denser public history. The 16 no-series withholds (all seafood plus ground-beef) are absent from every statistic. L = 33/37 is exempt from this concern: all 37 lock items cleared the join.

6. FLOAT n = 7. Every float-bucket number rests on seven ingredients. The Mann-Whitney withhold-vs-float test (p = 0.3038) is underpowered and its non-significance says nothing either way; it is the only member of the declared family of 7 that fails BH at q = 0.10.

7. THE WITHHOLD MEDIAN IS A BLENDED ARTIFACT. Reporting one median for the withhold bucket (0.1991) hides that it fuses two opposite populations — withhold/flat (n=10, median 0.108, degenerate near-flat series) and withhold/volatile (n=9, median 0.798). The pre-stated secondary direction held, but for exactly the compositional reason the hypothesis anticipated, so it is weak evidence.

8. UNITS ARE SAFE. Amplitude is a within-ingredient ratio and halfWidthPct is a fraction, so the carton/lb/sack/dozen per-package-unit trap does not apply. No cross-ingredient cents comparison was made anywhere.

9. HONESTY CONTRACT INTACT. halfWidthPct is a next-week reach, never contract-length drift, never a direction. Amplitude is a wholesale-reference within-year swing against each ingredient's own 5-year trailing normals, never a delivered price. Nothing here is a forecast, and no cause is asserted for any swing — this is a description of the tracked record as of the 2026-07-24 lockfloat asOf and the 2026-07-27 seasonality build.

10. NOT AUDITED: whether the site's published surfaces would actually mislead a reader. That is an editorial judgment, not a measurement. What is measured is only that the two numbers exist on two surfaces and stand in the stated ratio.

hypotheses.measuredResult:
A = 0 of 78. B = 78 of 78. The pre-registered kill condition ("FALSIFIED if 5 or fewer of the 78 tested anchors clear BH q=0.10") fired at zero.

SETUP. 80 anchors in co-movement.json; 2 excluded for an empty neighbours array (button-mushroom n=1, pork-belly n=1), leaving n=78 tested. My recomputation of cohort membership from data/cost-index-events.json reproduced co-movement.json's k and n EXACTLY for 80/80 anchors (zero-shift control), so the null machinery is verified against the shipped artifact.

OBSERVED. conc = maxK/n ranges 0.167 (1/6) to 1.000, median 0.400. Value counts: 2/6 ×33, 3/6 ×20, 4/6 ×5, 5/6 ×4, 2/5 ×3, 1/4 ×2, 1/3 ×2, 1/1 ×4, 6/6 ×2, 5/5 ×1, 1/2 ×1, 1/6 ×1.

NULL. 20,000 phase-preserving draws (5,000-draw run agreed to 3 decimals). Each non-anchor ingredient's event-date vector circular-shifted within its own observed span; anchor dates fixed; cohort recomputed with the detector's exact rule (same direction, |dt| <= 42 days, self excluded). Per-anchor null mean conc = 0.265 to 0.395 — i.e. a maximum over ~79 candidate partners lands near 2-of-6 BY CHANCE.

PER-ANCHOR TEST. Smallest p = 0.006050 (iceberg-lettuce). BH rank-1 critical value at q=0.10 is 0.10/78 = 0.001282 — the best anchor misses by 4.7x. Survivors: BH q=0.10 -> 0; BY q=0.10 -> 0; BH q=0.05 -> 0; BH q=0.20 -> 12; BY q=0.20 -> 0.

AGGREGATE TEST (not pre-registered, computed because the per-anchor test failed). Observed mean conc across the 78 anchors = 0.4833 vs null mean 0.3705. Dependence-preserving omnibus permutation p (mean conc recomputed on the same draw) = 0.000050 = 1/20001, the resolution floor. Excluding the duplicate pair: p = 0.000050. Uncorrected p<0.05 on 14/78 (null expectation 3.9); p<0.10 on 20/78 (expectation 7.8). Counterweight: 21 of 78 anchors are LESS concentrated than their own null mean.

STEP 5 (substitutes cross-check, run on all 78 anchors since there were no survivors). 214 top-partner pairs. 16 anchors absent from ingredient-depth.json; 186 top partners are not listed as substitutes at all; only 12 pairs carry a hedge verdict — 8 "mirror", 4 "hedge". The documented near-miss caused no join failure: salmon-skin-on-fillet has zero detected events and is not an anchor.
hypotheses.revisedClaim: Per-anchor co-mover persistence is NOT identifiable in the tracked record: zero of 78 testable anchors clear BH q=0.10 (or BY q=0.10, or BH q=0.05) against a phase-preserving null, the best anchor (iceberg-lettuce, p=0.0061) missing the rank-1 BH threshold of 0.0013 by 4.7x. The reason is that the null itself is concentrated — taking the maximum shared-episode count over ~79 candidate partners yields a mean conc of 0.37 by chance alone, so an observed 2-of-6 or 3-of-6 top partner (53 of 78 anchors) is exactly what independent episode timing produces. What IS measurable is the aggregate: mean concentration across the 78 anchors is 0.4833 against a null mean of 0.3705, omnibus permutation p = 0.00005 (1/20001, the floor at 20,000 draws), unchanged when the duplicate pair is removed. So the honest statement is population-level, not per-ingredient: co-movement is modestly but reliably more concentrated on repeat partners than chance timing allows, while 21 of 78 anchors are actually less concentrated than chance, and no individual pair can be named as a persistent partner at any defensible error rate. The site cannot convert this into a per-ingredient menu-construction rule.

Correctness control: zero-shift recomputation reproduced co-movement.json's full neighbour list and k for 80/80 anchors.
hypotheses.caveats:
SAMPLE SIZE IS SMALL AND COARSE. topN=6 caps every anchor at 6 episodes, so conc lives on a 6-point grid: 65 of 80 anchors have n=6, and 9 have n<=3. With max n=6 the statistic simply cannot resolve fine differences, and 4 of the 7 anchors at conc=1.0 have n=1, where a single co-occurring neighbour forces conc=1.0 arithmetically (mint's "top partner" is a 5-way tie at k=1).

DUPLICATE-SERIES ARTIFACT. ground-pork and pork-shoulder have byte-identical event vectors — same 6 dates, same 6 directions. Their mutual 6/6 is an aliased series, not co-movement. Excluding them left the omnibus p unchanged (0.000050), but any per-pair reading of them is a tautology.

CATALOG-GRANULARITY ARTIFACT, and it is the main threat to the aggregate result. The strongest anchors are four lettuce varieties (iceberg, romaine, red-leaf, green-leaf — 4 of the top 8), chicken-breast/chicken-thigh, and pork-shoulder/ground-pork. These are varieties or cuts of one commodity carried as separate slugs. The aggregate excess may largely measure how finely the ingredient catalog splits commodities rather than anything about market structure. I did not test that; a proper version would collapse varieties to a commodity level first.

SURVIVORSHIP. An ingredient needs >= 52 weekly observations (2 x BASE_WIN) before any event can be detected, and >= 3 distinct years for the season flag. 22 of 102 ingredients have zero events and never enter the anchor set; 2 more have no neighbours. The panel is therefore restricted to the longer, better-covered series.

NULL DESIGN LIMITS. The circular shift preserves each ingredient's episode count, internal spacing, and observation span, which correctly encodes the fact that recent-only series can only co-occur in recent years — that is why the null mean is as high as 0.37. It does NOT preserve seasonality: an ingredient whose episodes cluster in one calendar month gets shifted off that month, so shared seasonal timing is scored as signal rather than as baseline. That makes this null ANTI-conservative for the aggregate test, so the omnibus p=0.00005 is an upper bound on the evidence, not a lower one. A month-preserving null would be the stricter test and was not run.

NOT PRE-REGISTERED. The omnibus test was computed only after the pre-registered per-anchor test failed. It should be treated as exploratory and re-run under a stated threshold before anything is published.

NO CAUSAL CONTENT. Cohort membership is co-occurrence within +/-6 weeks and nothing else. Nothing here identifies a mechanism, a lead/lag, or a direction of influence, and the hypothesis's motivating use (do not build two dishes on a persistently-paired pair) is NOT supported per-ingredient by this result.

SUBSTITUTES CROSS-CHECK IS THIN. Only 12 of 214 top-partner pairs are listed substitutes at all (8 mirror, 4 hedge), and 16 anchors are missing from ingredient-depth.json entirely. The two agreements worth naming — chicken-breast -> chicken-thigh and green-leaf-lettuce -> red-leaf-lettuce, both already labelled "mirror" — are consistent with the co-movement data but rest on anchors that do not survive multiplicity control, so they confirm nothing.

kills.reasoning:

Provenance claims hold. `cheapest_month: c.worthTiming ? c.cheapMonth : null` at build-ingredient-state-record.mjs:553, and worthTiming at scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs:206-207 is a real two-part gate (a `robust` check plus `save >= TIMING_MIN_SAVE`), so calling it a noise gate is accurate, not decoration. Dropped slugs (eggs, sweet-potato, 6 months each) and the 14 ready-but-no-import exclusions match exactly.

The analysis is contract-clean: no causal verb, VALUE capitalized throughout, spec F correctly withheld on sign-instability, denominator on the record, twin calibration reported. The defects are confined to the revised claim's prose.

Defect 1 (value-to-volume slippage). The closing clause "which is exactly what the value-equals-price-times-quantity ambiguity predicts when neither component dominates" asserts a condition the instrument cannot evaluate. HS6 publishes no quantity; this panel measured zero quantity. Presenting the null as explained by that decomposition invites the reader to treat "neither component dominates" as established — affirming the consequent. The caveats state the same idea correctly in conditional form ("the EXPECTED result IF neither component dominates"); the claim states it as an explanation. Must be struck or restored to the conditional.

Defect 2 (overstated null). "carries no measurable information" and "the import-value calendar is uninformative" assert absence of relationship. With MDE 0.98 months this is a bounded null: any true advantage above about one month is excluded, anything smaller is unresolved. The bound appears two sentences later, which is the only thing saving the sentence; quoted alone, the opening and the closing verdict both overstate. Also, "confirming the test is calibrated rather than underpowered-by-construction" conflates Type-I calibration with power — the 4.4% twin rate shows the test can fire, not that it had power here; only the MDE speaks to power.

Defect 3 (fabricated correction premise — the most serious). I grepped the repo: "price-pressure calendar" and "volume proxy" appear ZERO times anywhere. /open/imports/ contains ZERO price references (medianCents, cents, wholesale, price normal, seasonality.json all 0 hits), so the hypothesis's motivating premise — "the site publishes the import calendar next to seasonal price normals on the same page" — is verifiably false. The live page already carries "never volume or delivered price", "Shown as association, never cause", "Value blends price and shipped quantity; the record stops at the last observed year and draws no forecast", and "it is not a forecast of any future month". The seasonality-fusion.mjs mechanism labels that DO link import phase to the cheap month ("Import-value counter-phase", "domestic-low") are dormant — only check-open-lane-honesty.mjs, check-seasonality-fusion.mjs and check-all.mjs reference the module, and no HTML file renders them. So the claim prescribes an "honest label" against two strawmen for a surface that is already contract-compliant, implying the instrument was mislabeling and is now self-correcting. On a brand built entirely on verified provenance, staging a correction to a framing never published is itself a provenance failure. The one genuine live over-read is a different sentence — the winter narration "It ships in precisely when the local field is bare", a supply verb attached to a value index, which breaks the fusion module's own "NO supply verbs" rule — but the panel tested price phase, not supply, so this finding cannot adjudicate that sentence either and must not be cited as doing so.

Not killed because all three defects are prose-level and a clean restatement exists: the bounded null on import-value peak phase versus wholesale price extrema, stated with its MDE, its wholesale-not-delivered qualifier, its gated-trough disclosure and its survivorship scope, violates nothing in the contract and is fully reproducible. Publication value is low once the strawman correction is removed — it corrects nothing live — but that is a novelty question, not an honesty one.
kills.requiredCaveat:
MANDATORY EXCISIONS before publication. (1) Strike "which is exactly what the value-equals-price-times-quantity ambiguity predicts when neither component dominates." HS6 publishes no quantity and this panel measured none; if the point is kept it must be strictly conditional and non-explanatory: "Import figures are nominal customs VALUE — price times quantity, with quantity unpublished at HS6 — so this panel cannot decompose the value calendar, and a null is consistent with, but is not evidence for, any particular balance of the two components." (2) Strike the relabeling clause "The honest label for the /open/imports/ calendar is therefore neither 'price-pressure calendar' nor 'volume proxy'." Neither phrase appears anywhere in the repo, /open/imports/ publishes no price normals, and the page already states "never volume or delivered price", "Shown as association, never cause", and "not a forecast of any future month". Publishing this implies a correction to a framing the site never made. Any live-surface implication must instead name the actual language it audits — and note that the seasonality-fusion.mjs "Import-value counter-phase" labels are dormant code, rendered on no page, and were NOT tested by this statistic. (3) Replace "carries no measurable information" and "the import-value calendar is uninformative" with the bounded form: "no phase relationship large enough for this panel to detect — any true mean advantage above about one month is ruled out (MDE 0.98 months at 80% power); anything smaller is unresolved." Drop "rather than underpowered-by-construction" from the twin sentence; a 4.4% Type-I rate shows the test can fire, not that it had power.

MANDATORY CAVEATS that must travel with the published text. (a) WHOLESALE, NOT DELIVERED: medianCents is a public wholesale reference against each ingredient's own trailing baseline window, in nominal cents per that ingredient's own trading unit; it is never what any restaurant pays. Extrema are computed within a single ingredient, so the unit trap does not affect the result. (b) GATED-TROUGH DISCLOSURE: the primary test uses the naive argmin of monthly medians, and Muntin's own worthTiming gate (scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs:206-207 — robustness plus save >= TIMING_MIN_SAVE) declines to certify a cheapest month for 19 of the 68 panel slugs. The instrument must not appear to publish a trough it withholds. State that restricting to the 49 gated slugs is also null (diff -0.306, p = 0.347) and that the naive argmin agreed with the gated cheapest_month on 49 of 49 where both exist. (c) ERA MISMATCH: import_seasonal_index is a mean over each ingredient's entire import series (2010-2025 for most), while seasonality months use a 5-year trailing window anchored to that series' latest print. The two calendars describe different eras; if import seasonality has shifted since 2010 this alone could produce the null. Untested. (d) SURVIVORSHIP: the panel is import-exposed produce plus a few beef/pork cuts. The 14 ready-but-excluded slugs (basil, chicken-breast, chicken-thigh, dill, mint, oregano, parsley, rosemary, short-rib, tarragon, thyme, vegetable-oil, whole-chicken, whole-turkey) are exactly the domestically supplied items where a harvest calendar would be cleanest. Does not generalise to the 100-slug catalog. (e) STRUCTURAL RESOLUTION LIMIT: the price peak and trough are not antipodal — mean separation 3.99 months, not 6.0 — so the paired contrast discriminates less than the design implies. (f) SPEC F MUST NOT BE PUBLISHED as a result: 1 of 10 defensible specs at p = 0.0444 is what alpha 0.05 buys for free, and the sign flips positive on specs H and I. (g) DENOMINATOR ON THE RECORD: 13 statistics computed against this panel (1 pre-stated test, 10 logged specs, 2 single-arm diagnostics); no correction applied because nothing survived uncorrected. (h) NO CAUSAL READING AND NO FORECAST: calendar co-occurrence between two independently derived calendars; nothing here says imports move price or price pulls imports, and nothing here is descriptive of any future month.

kills.reasoning:
I replicated every reported statistic exactly from source (PRIMARY rho=0.5190 p=0.0001 n=63; L=33/37 median ratio 6.390; within-lock +0.3030 p=0.072, within-cushion -0.0772, within-float -0.1071; bucket medians float 0.6266 > cushion 0.4221 > lock 0.2368 > withhold 0.1991). Provenance is clean: keysets exactly equal (100=100), null counts as stated, and I reconstructed the seasonality pipeline from raw series (data/cost-index.json + the deep store, 5-year own-latest-print window, >=2-distinct-year month gate) bit-exact against the committed file across 1038 month cells with 0 mismatches. The arithmetic is not in dispute. The inference is.

The finding never built the null model its own caveat 3 says it needs, and that omission is fatal rather than caveatable. I built it: a within-year exchangeability null that shuffles values among months WITHIN each year, preserving every year's level (so any multi-year trend or step survives completely intact) and every (year,month) observation count (so the >=2-distinct-year gate outcome is byte-identical). It destroys month-of-year alignment and nothing else. Four results, each independently sufficient to kill.

(1) THE PRE-REGISTERED FALSIFIER FOR THE SURVIVING CLAIM IS UN-FAILABLE. Expected L under the aseasonal null = 21.8 of 37. The pre-registration said "FALSIFIED if L < 19." A panel with literally zero calendar structure produces L ~= 22 and passes. Secondary 2 is the entire surviving headline of the revised claim, and it could not have failed. The 3x threshold has no null behind it: it compares a NEXT-WEEK conformal interval to a range over 12 monthly medians pooled across five years, and for any persistent series that ratio is large by time-aggregation alone. L=33 vs 21.8 is elevated, but the test as specified carries far less information than the write-up implies.

(2) ROUGHLY HALF THE HEADLINE "SWING" IS NULL-EXPECTED. Median observed amplitude 0.3350 vs median null-expected 0.1752 on the banded set (52%); for locks the median null/observed ratio is 0.534. max-min over 12 sample medians is an outward-biased order statistic (expected range of 12 iid draws ~3.26 sigma even under a flat truth), and the nominal 5-year window folds level drift into "amplitude." The revised claim's operator-facing "median lock band 4.4% against median annual swing 23.7%" therefore overstates calendar-attributable movement by roughly 2x.

(3) THE PRIMARY RHO IS ~94% MECHANICAL. rho(halfWidthPct, ASEASONAL-NULL amplitude) = +0.4856, permutation p=0.0003, against rho(halfWidthPct, observed amplitude) = +0.5190; the two amplitude vectors correlate at 0.833. An amplitude built from data with zero calendar content reproduces almost the entire primary statistic. So the pre-registered line "rho >= 0.5 with p < 0.05" is a test of shared volatility scaling between two summaries of one series, not a test of whether band width proxies season. The finding's declaration that "the orthogonality claim is dead by its own pre-registered line" fires on an artifact, and the revised claim then leads with that same artifact ("rho 0.52 ... enough shared signal that the two are not orthogonal"). Caveat 1 gestures at this qualitatively while still letting the kill stand; caveat 3 calls the inflation "unquantified." It is quantifiable and it is most of the effect. Note also that this collapses caveat 2's defense: the within-bucket rhos (+0.30, -0.08, -0.11) are the non-circular version and they are weak to absent, which is the finding's own admission that the between-bucket ordering carries no independent evidence.

(4) THE LEAD EXEMPLAR CONTRADICTS AN ALREADY-PUBLISHED MUNTIN HONESTY GATE. cost-index/menu-pricing.json returns cheapest_month=null for 11 of the 33 L-items: whole-turkey (50.7x), banana (19.6x), leek (14.8x), dill (9.3x), short-rib (6.4x), cabbage (4.4x), cheddar-cheese (4.0x), grapefruit (3.7x), red-onion (3.7x), pork-belly (3.6x), daikon (3.3x). The site's own published prose in scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs line 1257 names the flagship by name: "Whole turkey fails both - its monthly medians scatter and a typical January already undercuts a typical February - so it earns no window and prices year-round." The finding's single most dramatic number (whole turkey, 0.8% band vs 40.6% swing, 50.7x, quoted first in the revised claim) is exactly the reading Muntin's noise gate was built to suppress, and my independent null agrees with the site: null-median amplitude 0.3556 vs observed 0.4056, p = 0.176 - not distinguishable from an aseasonal series. Banana, the fourth named exemplar, is also gate-rejected. Two of the five named exemplars are ingredients Muntin has already declined to call seasonal. Of the 33, 5 (whole-turkey 0.176, dill 0.083, cheddar-cheese 0.624, red-onion 0.181, pork-belly 0.183) show no detectable calendar structure at all.

(5) THE EXTERNAL CROSS-CHECK IS SELECTION-BIASED AND NOT INDEPENDENT. "My argmin agrees with the published cheapest_month on 22 of 22" is 22 of 33: the 11 items the site's own gate REJECTED were silently dropped, and those are the informative cases. Validating only on the subset already certified and reporting 100% agreement inverts the test. It is also not independent evidence - both sides are computed from the same series.

What genuinely survives: 28 of 37 lock items do show p<0.05 calendar structure under my null, and L=33 does exceed the null's 21.8. There is real seasonality on this panel and the qualitative intuition ("lock is a statement about next week, not the calendar") is sound. But rescuing a publishable claim requires a noise-gated amplitude statistic, restriction to the 22 gate-passing items, and dropping the primary rho entirely - that is a different study, not a weakened version of this one. Publishing as written would put "whole turkey moves 40.6% across the year, a calendar problem" on one surface while a live surface says turkey "earns no window and prices year-round." On a brand built entirely on verified provenance, that self-contradiction is precisely the false positive this panel exists to prevent. Default-to-kill applies with room to spare.
kills.fatalProblem: "Amplitude" (max-min of 12 monthly medians over a 5-year nominal window) is not a seasonality statistic - it is an outward-biased order statistic that also absorbs trend, and the finding never built a null for it. Under a trend-preserving, count-preserving within-year exchangeability null: (a) expected L = 21.8/37, so the pre-registered falsifier "L < 19" sits BELOW the no-signal baseline and the surviving headline could not have failed; (b) median null-expected amplitude 0.1752 vs observed 0.3350, so ~52% of the reported "annual swing" is null-expected and the "23.7% median annual swing" is inflated ~2x; (c) rho(halfWidthPct, aseasonal-null amplitude) = +0.4856 vs +0.5190 observed (amplitude vectors correlate 0.833), so the primary statistic and the self-kill that fired on it are ~94% mechanical shared-volatility scaling, not seasonal information. Compounding this, the flagship exemplar contradicts a live Muntin gate: whole turkey (50.7x, quoted first) has cheapest_month=null in cost-index/menu-pricing.json and is named by name in the site's own published noise-gate prose at scripts/lib/cost-research.mjs:1257 as failing both noise tests and pricing "year-round" - my null concurs at p=0.176. 11 of the 33 L-items are gate-rejected, and the cross-check reported "22 of 22" after silently dropping exactly those 11.
kills.requiredCaveat: Not publishable in any form that reuses this amplitude definition. If a successor study is attempted, it MUST carry all of: (1) an explicit aseasonal null (within-year exchangeability, preserving year levels and per-month observation counts) reported alongside every amplitude, with the null-expected L stated next to the observed L - a falsifier threshold below the null baseline is not a falsifier; (2) per-ingredient seasonality p-values, with any item failing p<0.05 excluded from operator-facing counts and exemplars; (3) restriction to the 22 items that clear Muntin's OWN published noise gate (cheapest_month non-null in cost-index/menu-pricing.json), because publishing a "calendar swing" for an ingredient the site declares "prices year-round" is a live self-contradiction - whole turkey and banana must never appear as exemplars; (4) removal of the primary Spearman entirely, or its restatement as measuring shared volatility scaling only, given rho=+0.486 against zero-seasonality data; (5) amplitude reported as excess-over-null, not raw max-min, and deflated or trend-decomposed before any multi-year window is used (russet-potato's 111.5% is not a clean annual cycle); (6) the cross-check reported on the full 33, disclosing the 11 gate-rejections, and labeled as an internal consistency check rather than external validation, since both sides derive from the same series.

kills.reasoning:
The primary claim is already falsified by the researcher's own probe (D3=7 vs null [4,10], p=0.567 on the independence-respecting framing). My job was the revised claim, and it fails harder than the original — the boring explanation is not just "three layers share a file," it is "four of the five layers measure Muntin's own configuration."

STRUCTURE FIRST. I reproduced the matrix. The 21-item "dark set" contains exactly TWO distinct layer vectors with zero within-group variation: 16 slugs at [BAND 0, SEASON 0, YIELD 1, TRADE 1, EVENTS 0] and 5 herbs at [0,1,1,0,0]. D=21 vs null95=7 is not evidence of concentration; it is arithmetic on two upstream conditions. Any test that treats 21 slugs as 21 draws is answering a question with n=2.

MECHANISM A IS NOT A PUBLIC-RECORD GAP — IT IS A FETCH-WINDOW SETTING AND A DELIBERATE REFUSAL. data/cost-index-sources.json shrimp.noaa = {"basis":"index","years":2,"_report":"NOAA FOSS trade_data IMPORT unit value. basis:index (DIRECTIONAL ONLY, no dollar level) — commodity shrimp import value runs ~$1.6-2.3/lb, at/below the 250c floor, so a $ level would be rejected or misleadingly cheap."} Every one of the 15 seafood slugs' history rows carries basis "customs" — an import unit value. So (i) BAND is withheld because the instrument correctly declines to price off trade data; that is the honesty contract WORKING, relabeled as a coverage failure. (ii) "years": 2 is a configured window; the series runs 2025-02→2026-04. The seasonality gate then fails in Muntin's own words — blocker = "need 6 months proven across 2+ years (have 3)" — i.e. SEASON is not an independent layer, it is a history-length assertion about the same configured window. (iii) EVENTS follows mechanically. Three "layer failures," one setting. Meanwhile the public record for these species is deep: the repo's own data/census-imports.jsonl spans 2010–2025 (2,641 records, 117–177/yr). Publishing "these 16 have no wholesale reference at all" attributes a fetch-window choice to the public record. That is the exact error class the honesty contract exists to prevent.

Worse for the "independent layers" story: for these 16, the price series and the TRADE layer come from the SAME customs universe. The population-level phi (TRADE independent, |φ|≤0.18) averages over a dark-set core where price IS trade.

MECHANISM B IS A QUOTATION-GRID AND ESTIMATOR ARTIFACT, AND THE PROSE IS FACTUALLY WRONG. The herb entries are reducer "mostlyMid", unit "carton" — the midpoint of an AMS terminal "mostly" range on a ~$7.50 carton, where a single $0.50 tick is 6.7%. The claim's phrase "an administered, effectively non-varying print" is false: basil 600→800 (+33%), thyme 1325→1050 (−20.8%), rosemary 750→850 (+13.3%) inside the window. These prices move a lot; they move rarely and in coarse steps. halfWidthPct=0 is a property of a percentile band estimator on a step function (median weekly change = 0), and eventCount=0 is Muntin's own 20%-vs-3-week-smoothed-±26-week-normal floor with n=130 over 2.5 years. Nothing here is a fact about herb markets. Calling it non-varying inverts the honesty contract's own rule against reading absence as a market property.

THE TRADE LAYER IS AN AUTHORING BACKLOG. data/ingredient-hs-codes.json carries a live _pending block (resolved_2026_07 for whole-salmon/halibut/trout). The 14 unmapped slugs include chicken-breast, whole-chicken, whole-turkey, vegetable-oil — all with unambiguous HS6 codes (0207, 1507–1515). TRADE measures crosswalk completeness. YIELD is a book table. So of five "layers": three are one fetch window, one is a to-do list, one is a reference table.

FACTUAL ERROR IN THE REVISED CLAIM ITSELF. It states "every one of the 100 carries an edible-yield figure." It is 96/100 — butter, cheddar-cheese, eggs and vegetable-oil are absent from ingredient-yields.json (118 rows; nearest slugs are eggplant, butternut-squash, butter-lettuce). The finding's own provenance section says 96. A claim that contradicts its own provenance cannot ship on a provenance brand.

WHAT IS LEFT. Only a methods disclosure: the 37 withholds fall into two shapes, both of which are the instrument declining. That content already exists as data/cost-lockfloat.json items[slug].reason (no-series / flat / volatile) — the study's own testSpec names that field as the canonical distinction. Re-presenting it plus a known HS backlog is not a discovery; the surprisingness score of 2 is if anything generous. The genuine publishable negative ("no tracked ingredient is dark from every angle") is also weakened, because the honest reason is not "the layers are independent" but "three of the five were never separate layers."

Verdict: kill. The statistical claim is falsified on its own honest re-test, the mechanism narrative misattributes Muntin's configuration to the public record in three places, and one sentence of the revised claim is flatly false against the files it cites.

kills.reasoning:
I reproduced every headline number exactly (eligible 80, A=10, B=61, holdout medians 0.039216 / 0.725490, discovery 0.058824 / 0.764706) and then tried to kill it four ways. The main gap survived all four; the contamination sub-claim did not survive one.

WHAT I COULD NOT KILL (main gap):
(1) Desk confound — the finding's caveat 4 says "I did not stratify by desk — n is too small to." That is wrong; the stratification is trivial and I ran it. Every desk holding both groups reproduces the gap: usda-ams-boston A=6 med 0.0294 vs B=18 med 0.5490; usda-ams-los-angeles A=3 med 0.1569 vs B=25 med 0.6667; usda-ams-miami A=1 0.2157 vs B=1 0.8627. A within-desk stratified permutation (20,000 draws, permuting only inside desk) gives 0/20,000 >= observed. The desk-artifact confound is refuted, not merely unaddressed.
(2) Short-history/new-series confound — the 7 Group B slugs with <200 rows (bok-choy, cilantro, daikon, dill, ginger, mint, whole-turkey) have holdout median 0.5686, nowhere near Group A. Recency of ingestion does not produce stickiness.
(3) Deep out-of-sample — the finding only checked the adjacent 52 rows. I went further back: rows -260..-209 (~5y) gives A(n=5) 0.1373 vs B(n=51) 0.7647; rows -520..-469 (~10y) gives A 0.3333 vs B 0.9020. The separation persists a decade back and only dissolves at the 2001-02 horizon the finding cites. Its regime caveat is directionally right but overstates how fast the effect decays — and rests on n=5, since the other five Group A members have no pre-2024 history at all.
(4) Effect size is not trivial and not noise-adjacent under any framing.

WHAT I DID KILL:
(A) PSEUDO-REPLICATION — the reported n is false and the headline number is inflated. Group A is not 10 independent series. Five of the ten are fresh herbs — basil, oregano, rosemary, tarragon, thyme — all usda-ams-boston, all carton, all n=130, all with the identical series start 2024-01-10. That is one AMS report block ingested as one event, not five draws. Their change weeks are partly synchronized (oregano and thyme both move at pair-positions 28-29; oregano and rosemary both at 18). They occupy five of the six lowest ranks in Group A and therefore *determine* the reported median. Drop them and A's median moves 0.0392 -> 0.1569 (holdout) and 0.0588 -> 0.1569 (discovery): the published 13x ratio (5.9% vs 76.5%) becomes 4.9x (15.7% vs 76.5%). The slug-level permutation assumes ten exchangeable units; effective n is ~5-6. Collapsing the herb block to a single unit (A=6) still gives medA 0.0980 vs medB 0.7255, p=0.00005 — so the inference lives, but the number as written does not. Caveat 3's "small n, loudly — Group A is 10 series" is the wrong disclosure of the wrong n.
(B) THE CONTAMINATION SUB-CLAIM IS DEFINITIONALLY CIRCULAR — fatal, must be struck. 'flat' and 'lock' are not independent rules; they are two thresholds on the same statistic. cost-conformal.js:158 sets degenerate = halfWidthPct < 0.003; cost-lockfloat.js:32-35,74 sets lock = halfWidthPct <= 0.08 AND coverageLo >= 0.60. halfWidthPct is a residual-quantile spread and is monotone-ish in quote-change rate (Spearman rho = 0.477 across Group B). So "the published lock bucket is contaminated by administratively sticky quotes" reduces to "0.003 < hw <= 0.08 lies between 0 and 0.08." Check the eight named items' own hw values: banana 0.006, cilantro 0.012, pear 0.013, leek 0.015, poblano-pepper 0.029, habanero-pepper 0.039, daikon 0.044, butter-lettuce 0.058 — every one sits in the bottom band, four of them within 5x of the flat cutoff itself. Of course all eight are locks. The reported "P(8 lowest all lock | random) = 0.008" is meaningless because bucket assignment is not random with respect to the test statistic — it is the same function of the same residuals. There is also threshold shopping: the pre-registered spec says <=0.25 and yields C=2; the claim's wording says "<= the flat set's worst member," a data-dependent order statistic (kale, 0.3333) drawn from a group half-composed of pseudo-replicates, and yields C=8 — and it is the 8 that gets published. Worse, the module's own header comment already documents this ("a flat/stale window yields a ~zero-width band"), so presenting it as a self-critical discovery about the site misrepresents the codebase.
(C) The circularity the finding does admit is tighter than it says. In the labeling window itself (last 27 observations) Group A's max change rate is 0.1538 and Group B's min is 0.1538 — the two groups touch at exactly one point. The label is, to a very good approximation, a change-rate threshold. The "discovery" window is therefore not an independent construct either; it is adjacent-window persistence of the same statistic. That is a real result, but it is a persistence result, not a validation result, and it must be described as such.

Net: the descriptive gap is robust and publishable; the number attached to it is not, and the second half of the claim is a restatement of the classifier's own thresholds.

The finding kills its own headline (the tautology control is correct and I confirm it is tighter than stated), then substitutes a fallback it calls "the real and much larger audit finding." That fallback is a pure arithmetic artifact of muntin's own estimator. I reproduced it on data with no market in it at all.

1. THE FALLBACK UNDERCOVERAGE FINDING IS THE QUANTILE CONVENTION, NOT THE INSTRUMENT.
/home/user/potentially-profitable/tools/_shared/cost-conformal.js lines 43-50 define `quantile()` as a plain type-7 sample quantile — `idx=(n-1)*p`, linear interpolation — with NO split-conformal (n+1) finite-sample correction. `intervalFromResiduals` (line 62) takes `recent = resid.slice(-window)` with the default `window = 26` and `alpha = 0.20` (lines 137-139), and `scripts/build-cost-lockfloat.mjs:89` calls `conformalNext(vals)` with no opts, so calibrate is off and scale = 1 — the published band IS the raw band.

Analytically: n = 26, alpha = 0.2. Lower bound sits at type-7 index (26-1)(0.1) = 2.5, i.e. interpolated between order statistics 3 and 4; for an exchangeable new draw P(X_new < X_(k)) = k/(n+1) = k/27, so lower-tail miscoverage is between 3/27 = 11.1% and 4/27 = 14.8%, about 12.9%. The upper bound at index 22.5 is symmetric. Expected coverage ≈ 100% − 25.9% = 74.1%, not 80%.

I ran the EXACT code path (same quantile fn, same backtest loop, window 26, minResid 8, scale 1, series length 1,047 ≈ 65,932/63) on synthetic series, 300 replications each:
• iid Gaussian random walk: pooled 74.97%, median 75.14%, min 73.51%, max 75.92%, 100% of series below 0.80
• iid t(4) heavy-tailed increments: pooled 74.53%, median 74.47%, min 73.22%, max 76.01%, 100% below 0.80
• Gaussian + drift: pooled 74.98%. Mild heteroskedasticity: pooled 74.65%
• short series (n = 120, the observed minimum nTested): pooled 74.38%, min 67.57%, max 80.18%, 99.3% below 0.80

Observed on the real data (I re-derived it from data/cost-lockfloat.json): mean 74.64%, pooled 74.47%, median 74.70%, min 65.40%, max 80.20%, 62/63 below 0.80, 52/63 with Wilson CI entirely below, 0 above; nTested min 120, median 1,304, max 1,305, sum 65,932.

The real numbers sit BETWEEN the Gaussian and t(4) nulls — exactly where heavy-tailed food prices should land — and the observed spread (65.4%–80.2%) is bracketed by the short-series null (67.6%–80.2%). "62 of 63 fall short of 80%" is not an audit discovery; it is the deterministic output of this estimator on anything exchangeable. The boring explanation does not merely fit as well as the interesting one, it fits to within half a percentage point, with an analytic derivation behind it.

2. THE 80% TARGET IS NOT EVEN PUBLISHED. `grep -c "80%" tools/cost-pulse/index.html` returns 0. The four "target" hits are a WCAG comment and JS DOM selectors. The "target 80%, held X%" phrasing the hypothesis quoted lives ONLY in a cost-conformal.js docblock comment (lines 21-23) as a suggestion for what a card *could* say. Publishing "the band misses its promise" would be a manufactured self-indictment — precisely the false positive that damages a provenance brand.

3. THE POST-HOC ONSET RESIDUE IS THE TIGHTEST TAUTOLOGY OF ALL, NOT THE SURVIVOR. The band's residual window is ALSO 26. Same window length, same series, same file of prices. An event onset is by construction a point that departs ≥20% from a median containing the 26 weeks before it, i.e. it is definitionally preceded by a quiet run — which is exactly the 26 residuals the band is calibrated on at that instant. "Narrow band immediately before a detected departure" is the joint definition of the two objects, not a measured property. The complement result the finding reports (duration-minus-onset, 1.073x) is the same mechanism running the other way: once the big move enters the 26-week residual window the band widens. The finding's caveat 2 half-concedes this, then still calls onset "the one place an episode effect does survive." It does not survive; it is the least separable of the three.

What is genuinely left is an internal engineering ticket, not a publication: the band's true nominal at window = 26 with this quantile convention is ~74%, so either apply the conformal correction (use the ceil((n+1)(1−alpha)) order statistic) or restate the target. That is real and worth fixing, but it is the OPPOSITE of the finding's framing — the instrument is not underperforming its promise; the internal label is mis-specified, and the shipped card already reports only the achieved rate, honestly.
