MECHANISM 1 — THE "SEASONAL AMPLITUDE" VARIABLE IS NOT SEASONAL. I built a phase-randomized null: for each ingredient I took the exact 5-year trailing window the build uses, held the date vector fixed, and circularly rotated the value vector against it. This preserves every observed value, the serial correlation, the trend, the level regime, and the volatility exactly; it destroys only calendar alignment. If amplitude measured season, observed amplitude must beat this null. It does not.

- rho(halfWidthPct, OBSERVED amplitude) = 0.5190 (reproduces the finding exactly).
- rho(halfWidthPct, PHASE-NULL amplitude) = 0.5334. The primary correlation is fully reproduced — slightly stronger — with the calendar removed entirely.
- rho(observed amplitude, phase-null amplitude) = 0.9171. The published "seasonal amplitude" shares 84% of its rank variance with a quantity that has no calendar content.
- L (lock items with amplitude > 3x halfWidth) = 33/37 observed vs 34/37 under the null. The headline number is BELOW its own null.
- Median ratio 6.35 observed vs 5.98 null. The finding's "median 6.4x" is 6.0x with no seasonality present.
- Only 1 of 37 lock items (striploin, p=0.017) exceeds its own phase null at p<0.05 — exactly the chance yield of 37 tests at alpha=0.05, and it fails the finding's own declared BH correction.
- The four named exemplars are the worst offenders, not the best: whole-turkey obs 0.406 vs null 0.417, p=0.581; banana 0.118 vs 0.111, p=0.312; cilantro 0.219 vs 0.201, p=0.312; red-potato 0.305 vs 0.218, p=0.152. Every headline sentence in the revised claim rests on an ingredient whose "annual swing" is statistically indistinguishable from calendar noise.

MECHANISM 2 — HORIZON TAUTOLOGY (the metric contains the thing it "predicts"). Reading tools/_shared/cost-conformal.js: halfWidthPct is the alpha=0.20 half-reach of ONE-STEP residuals taken from only the last 26 residuals (window: 26, resid.slice(-window)), divided by the LAST print. Amplitude is a range statistic over 5 YEARS of pooled levels. The module states outright that its predictor is a random walk ("a random-walk (last-value) predictor"). For a random walk the level range over T steps scales as sigma*sqrt(T); at T ~ 260 weeks that is a 16-25x multiple of the one-step reach before any seasonality exists. So "amplitude > 3 x halfWidthPct" is near-certain for every non-degenerate series by construction. Secondary 2 restates "a one-week band is narrower than a five-year range." The null confirms the magnitude: 34/37 with the calendar deleted.

MECHANISM 3 — THE BAND WINDOW IS SEASONALLY LOCATED AND, FOR THE LEAD EXAMPLE, EXCLUDES THE SEASON. whole-turkey's 26-residual conformal window spans 2025-12-15 to 2026-06-22. It contains months 01,02,03,04,05,06,12 and excludes 07,08,09,10,11 outright — the entire Thanksgiving run-up a reader would assume the "40.6% swing" names. Every lock item's halfWidthPct on this build is a Dec-Jun statistic. Comparing it to a full-calendar quantity is not apples-to-apples even in principle, independent of Mechanism 1.

WHAT THE FINDING ALREADY CONCEDED, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. Caveat 1 correctly identifies the shared-input channel and caveat 2 correctly voids Secondary 1 as the primary re-binned by half-width thresholds. But caveat 1 is stated as a reason to soften the interpretation of rho, while the revised claim still calls the y-variable "seasonal amplitude" and still leads with "swing more than three times their own band width across the calendar year." The words "seasonal" and "across the calendar year" are precisely the unearned part, and the finding never tested them. Caveat 3 (trend absorbed into amplitude) is confirmed and severe — russet-potato obs 1.115 vs null 0.570 — but the finding calls it "unquantified"; it is now quantified, and it does not rescue anything.

THE EXTERNAL CROSS-CHECK IS NOT INDEPENDENT. "My argmin month agrees with published cheapest_month on 22 of 22" recomputes the same statistic from the same file that produced the published field. That verifies reproducibility, not seasonality, and it cannot corroborate the claim.

The primary was already dead by pre-registration (rho 0.5190 >= 0.500, p = 0.0001). The only piece the finding proposed to publish — Secondary 2 — is dead by a null it never ran. Nothing survives that is simultaneously true and non-trivial.

NOTHING HERE VIOLATES THE HONESTY CONTRACT — no forecast, no cause, no delivered-price confusion, units are safe within-ingredient ratios. The finding is honest. It is simply measuring an artifact.

UPSTREAM FLAG, NOT PART OF THIS VERDICT: the same phase-null result implies data/seasonality.json's monthly-median amplitudes may not be distinguishable from calendar noise for most ingredients, which would touch the published cheapest_month / save_pct fields in cost-index/menu-pricing.json (save_pct median 26%). I did NOT audit the noise gate that field passes through, so I make no claim about it — but it deserves its own test. That would be a genuine, publishable, correction-forcing finding. It is a different finding from this one.
kills.fatalProblem: The dependent variable is not seasonal. A phase-randomized null (values circularly rotated against fixed dates — preserving every value, the trend, the autocorrelation and the volatility, destroying only calendar alignment) reproduces the entire result: rho(halfWidth, null-amplitude) = 0.5334 vs 0.5190 observed; L = 34/37 under the null vs 33/37 observed; median ratio 5.98 vs 6.35; and observed amplitude correlates 0.9171 with its own calendar-free counterpart. Only 1 of 37 lock items beats its own null at p<0.05 (chance expectation for 37 tests). The four named exemplars are the weakest cases: whole-turkey p=0.581, banana p=0.312, cilantro p=0.312, red-potato p=0.152. Compounding this, halfWidthPct is a ONE-STEP reach computed from only the last 26 residuals (cost-conformal.js window:26) divided by the last print, while amplitude is a 5-year range statistic — under the random-walk predictor the module explicitly declares, a 16-25x ratio is guaranteed by horizon mismatch alone. "33 of 37 lock ingredients swing more than 3x their band" is a restatement of "a one-week band is narrower than a five-year range," which is true of every non-degenerate price series and carries no calendar information.
kills.requiredCaveat: Do not publish. If any fragment is ever revived, it may not use the word "seasonal", "annual", or "across the calendar year" for the (max-min)/median of 12 monthly medians unless that quantity is first shown to exceed a phase-randomized null per ingredient — on this panel it does not, for 36 of 37 lock items. Any revived version must also state that halfWidthPct is measured from only the last 26 one-step residuals (a Dec-2025-to-Jun-2026 window on this build) and is therefore not commensurable with a full-calendar range statistic; for whole-turkey specifically the band window excludes months 07-11 entirely, so the "0.8% band vs 40.6% swing" contrast cannot be attributed to the ingredient's behaviour. Finally, the menu-pricing.json cheapest_month cross-check must not be described as independent corroboration — it recomputes the same statistic from the same substrate.

kills.reasoning:
I went looking for the specific statistic and could not find it published — and then found that both halves of the novelty claim are false anyway, one externally and one inside this repo.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNPUBLISHED. I could find no source computing a circular-month phase contrast between an import-VALUE seasonal index and a wholesale-price seasonal index across an ingredient panel (mean circ distance to price argmax vs price argmin, permutation null). Not in ERS, not in JAAE/AJAE/AgEcon, not in Flexport/CoBank/trade press. The number 2.8382 vs 2.9118 months (diff -0.0735, permutation p = 0.7199 two-sided, k = 32/31/5 of 68) is new. That is the only thing here that is new.

EXTERNAL PRIOR ART #1 — THE "UNRESOLVED AMBIGUITY" WAS RESOLVED IN 1999. whyNovel asserts the value-vs-volume reading is unresolvable because "Nothing on the site — or anywhere public — resolves which reading the data actually supports." That is wrong. Alterman, Diewert & Feenstra (1999), "International Trade Price Indexes and Seasonal Commodities" (BLS), measured it directly for U.S. trade: over Sept 1993–Dec 1996, between 23 and 40 percent of U.S. import and export lines exhibited seasonal variation in QUANTITIES, while only about 5 percent exhibited seasonal variation in PRICES. That result is canonical enough to be reproduced verbatim in three international statistical manuals — IMF XMPI Manual ch.23 (Treatment of Seasonal Products), IMF PPI Manual ch.22, ILO CPI Manual ch.22 — and re-cited in Diewert's 2022 UBC discussion paper on seasonal products. The published answer to "is a customs-value seasonal peak a price event or a volume event" is: overwhelmingly a volume event. This is not a subtlety; it is textbook trade-statistics guidance the finding claims does not exist.

That prior art also directly contradicts the revised claim's punchline. The revised claim ends "the honest label ... is therefore neither 'price-pressure calendar' nor 'volume proxy'." The panel measured no volume series at all — HS6 quantity was never in the join — so the "not a volume proxy" half is unlicensed by the test, and it happens to point the wrong way against the one published measurement that does address it. Publishing that sentence would put muntin in print against the IMF/ILO manuals on a question it did not test. For a brand whose entire value is verified provenance, that is worse than publishing nothing.

EXTERNAL PRIOR ART #2 — THE NULL IS THE LITERATURE'S PREDICTION, WITH A MECHANISM. The qualitative phase question is not open. ERS FTS-357-01, "Evolving U.S. Fruit Markets and Seasonal Grower Price Patterns" (five fresh-fruit markets, 1980–2012), states that imports arriving in the low-domestic-supply fall/winter months have produced "more consistent year-round availability and lower off-season prices" — i.e. imports have smoothed the very price peak they arrive into. ERS Amber Waves (Oct 2014, strawberries vs apples) reports "persistence of seasonality in strawberry prices, but some smoothing of apple price fluctuations over time." Raper, Thornsbury & Aguilar, JAAE 41(1) 2009, "Regional Wholesale Price Relationships in the Presence of Counter-Seasonal Imports," builds its whole VAR design on a regime split between domestic-supply-dominated and counter-seasonal-import-dominated periods in the fresh peach wholesale market. And the JAAE "Imported Challenge" line of work documents the post-2010 shift in which imports increasingly compete DURING domestic harvest seasons rather than only around them. Taken together the published record already says: the import calendar used to sit in the high-price off-season, imports then flattened that peak, and imports have since moved into the harvest window too — so no stable modern phase relation should be expected. A measured null on a 5-year trailing price window is what that literature predicts, not a discovery against it.

INTERNAL PRIOR ART #3 — THE "CORRECTION" IS ALREADY SHIPPED, ON THE EXACT PAGE. This is the one that ends it. whyItMatters claims the site publishes the import calendar in a framing that "invites a backwards buying decision" and that a null "forces a correction." I read the live page. /home/user/potentially-profitable/open/imports/index.html already states, in four separate places: "Nominal customs value — price × quantity, not a delivered price."; "Import figures are nominal customs value — they blend price and quantity (quantity is unpublished at HS6) and are never a delivered or retail price."; and in the meta/JSON-LD description "US food imports by value (nominal customs dollars, never volume or delivered price)". The page already refuses BOTH readings the finding proposes to adjudicate. The revised claim's conclusion is the label the page has been shipping.

The engine agrees. /home/user/potentially-profitable/scripts/lib/seasonality-fusion.mjs, header contract lines 10–22, already codifies it as a binding rule: "import_seasonal_index is import *VALUE* seasonality — never volume, tonnage, or supply share. Labels describe two price/value CALENDARS in phase, never a supply flow. Banned verbs: supplies/supplied/backfill/fills the gap/tonnage/volume," and "'Domestic-season low' is inferred-from-phase, never asserted as a measured harvest calendar." There is no live over-claim for this null to correct.

DOES IT AT LEAST AUDIT THE ONE LIVE PHASE FIELD? No — and I checked. The live per-ingredient chip comes from mechanismFor(), whose counter-phase test is idx[cheapMonth-1] >= 1.05: "is import value elevated above its own mean in the month the domestic reference troughs." The finding instead measured circular distance from the import ARGMAX to the price argmax vs argmin. Those are different statistics on different quantities, and the finding's own caveats concede the paired contrast is blunt (price peak and trough sit only 3.99 months apart on this panel, not 6.0). So the null does not refute the counter-phase label either. It audits nothing that ships.

WHAT SURVIVES AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. The analysis itself is clean — the phase-randomised twin at 4.4% two-sided confirms calibration, the 10-spec multiverse is honest, the single p = 0.0444 hit (spec F, p75Cents) is correctly withheld under sign instability given specs H and I flip positive, and the MDE of 0.98 months honestly bounds the null rather than proving zero. None of that is in dispute. But under this lens the test is: is the thing we would publish already known? The publishable sentence is "you cannot read the import-value calendar as a price calendar." That sentence is (a) the direct implication of a 1999 BLS result enshrined in three UN-family statistical manuals, (b) the mechanism ERS has been describing since at least 2014, and (c) already printed four times on muntin's own /open/imports/ page. A precise number attached to an already-published conclusion is context, not a finding. Kill.
kills.fatalProblem: The novelty premise is false on both halves. Externally: whyNovel claims nothing public resolves the import-value-vs-volume reading, but Alterman, Diewert & Feenstra (1999) measured it for U.S. trade — 23-40% of import/export lines show seasonal QUANTITY variation vs ~5% seasonal PRICE variation — a result reproduced as canonical guidance in IMF XMPI Manual ch.23, IMF PPI Manual ch.22 and ILO CPI Manual ch.22, and the revised claim's "neither ... nor 'volume proxy'" clause contradicts it on a quantity dimension this test never measured. Internally: the "correction" the null claims to force is already shipped — /home/user/potentially-profitable/open/imports/index.html already prints "Nominal customs value — price × quantity, not a delivered price" and "never a delivered or retail price," and /home/user/potentially-profitable/scripts/lib/seasonality-fusion.mjs lines 10-22 already bind the engine to "never volume, tonnage, or supply share ... never a supply flow." There is no live over-claim to refute and no unknown to resolve.
kills.requiredCaveat: If any of this is reused as internal context or a methods/limitations note on /open/imports/ (NOT as a finding), it must: (1) drop the "neither a price-pressure calendar nor a volume proxy" clause entirely — no volume or HS6 quantity series entered the join, so the volume half is unmeasured, and the one published measurement that bears on it (Alterman, Diewert & Feenstra 1999, via IMF XMPI Manual ch.23 / IMF PPI Manual ch.22 / ILO CPI Manual ch.22: 23-40% of U.S. trade lines seasonal in quantity vs ~5% in price) points toward quantity dominance, not away from it; (2) cite the prior art it is reproducing rather than framing the null as new — ERS FTS-357-01 "Evolving U.S. Fruit Markets and Seasonal Grower Price Patterns" (counter-seasonal imports have lowered/smoothed off-season prices), ERS Amber Waves Oct 2014 (strawberry seasonality persists, apple smooths), Raper/Thornsbury/Aguilar JAAE 41(1) 2009 on counter-seasonal-import price regimes; (3) state that it does not test the live counter-phase chip, whose rule is idx[cheapMonth-1] >= 1.05 in seasonality-fusion.mjs, not an argmax-distance contrast; and (4) carry the bounded-null language verbatim — n = 68 (not the spec's asserted 70), MDE 0.98 months at 80% power, so nothing smaller than roughly one calendar month is resolvable, and the lone p = 0.0444 spec-F hit is a 1-in-10 forking-path artifact with sign flips on specs H and I and must not be quoted as a result.

kills.fatalProblem:
The headline null is an arithmetic cancellation of two opposite-signed subpopulations created by heterogeneous data vintage, not an absence of structure — and the finding's framing conceals this.

`import_seasonal_index` history length across the 68-slug panel is sharply bimodal: 23 slugs rest on 3-4 years of monthly Census data, 40 rest on 14-16 years, 5 in between (histogram: 1 slug 0y, 14 at 3y, 8 at 4y, 1 at 5y, 1 at 8y, 3 at 9y, 6 at 14y, 1 at 15y, 33 at 16y). The short-history group is exactly the 10-digit HTS statistical suffixes this repo only pulled from 2022/2023 onward (0702002019 cherry-tomato, 0705192020/0705194020 romaine, 0709932020 zucchini, 0704904022 broccoli, 0709602020 jalapeno), several of them DATE-WINDOWED tariff lines whose per-calendar-month observation counts are badly unbalanced — cherry-tomato's are [8,8,12,12,12,12,22,22,22,22,24,24].

Splitting on that boundary, with the published index and no other change to the finding's own pipeline:
  - >=10y import history: n=40, diff = -0.700, k=22/38, permutation p2 = 0.0981 (PREDICTED direction)
  - <10y import history:  n=28, diff = +0.821, k=10/25, permutation p2 = 0.0722 (OPPOSITE direction)
  - pooled (the published result): n=68, diff = -0.074, p2 = 0.722
(40 x -0.700 + 28 x +0.821) / 68 = -0.074. The published null is reproduced to three decimals as the weighted average of two opposing halves. The partition is not a forking path: every history threshold from 6y through 14y returns the identical 40/28 split, because the distribution is degenerate there.

This makes two load-bearing sentences of the revisedClaim false as applied. (a) "the month of peak import VALUE carries no measurable information about where either the priciest or the cheapest month sits" — it is uninformative in aggregate BECAUSE the panel is not one population, which is a different statement about a different object. (b) "The panel can rule out any true phase advantage larger than about one month in either direction (MDE 0.98 months)" — one subgroup's point estimate is 0.70 months and the other's is 0.82 months, in OPPOSITE directions; the exclusion band exists only in the average of opposing effects. That is the most quotable line in the finding and it misleads.

Separately, the finding declares the hypothesis "refuted" without running a correction its own honesty logic demands. `import_seasonal_index` pools 2010-2025; `data/seasonality.json` uses windowYears=5 (params confirmed in the file header, generatedFrom 2026-07-27). The finding caveats this era mismatch and says "I did not test that." It is testable in-repo from data/census-imports.jsonl. Recomputing the import index on the matched 2021-2025 window: full panel n=67, diff = -0.209, p2 = 0.525 (still null), but on the long-history subset n=40, diff = -0.900, permutation p2 = 0.0316 — in the ORIGINALLY PREDICTED direction. Commensurability of estimation windows is exactly the rule Muntin applies to its own longitudinal spine ("honest week-over-week only across commensurable editions"). A hypothesis that survives at p=0.03 under a preregisterable commensurability fix is "not established," not "refuted."

The escape hatch on the other side is also closed. The >=10y group is dominated by counter-seasonal winter-import produce (avocado, asparagus, grapefruit, lemon, lime, cantaloupe, watermelon, cucumber, tomato). If that -0.700/-0.900 signal is real, its content is the already-published ERS fact that US produce imports peak in the northern winter when domestic supply is absent and wholesale price is high — which the hypothesis's own whyNovel concedes is "thoroughly published." So the panel resolves to: pooled result = artifact of cancellation; long-history arm = underpowered restatement of a known qualitative fact; short-history arm = 3-year argmax noise. No publishable content survives in any arm.
kills.reasoning:
I replicated the primary statistic independently from the two source files and matched it exactly: mean d_peak = 2.838, d_trough = 2.912, diff = -0.074, k = 32/63 non-tied, permutation p2 = 0.7219. The provenance block is accurate on every point I could check — the join really is on `key` not `slug`, n really is 68 not 70, `import_seasonal_index` really is built at scripts/build-ingredient-state-record.mjs by `meanMonth[mo]/av` with index 0 = January, there really are 21 malformed lines in data/census-imports.jsonl, and no honesty-contract clause is violated anywhere (value-not-volume, wholesale-not-delivered, co-occurrence-not-cause, no forecast are all handled correctly). This is careful work and the kill is not about sloppiness.

My lens is alternative-explanation, so I went looking for construction artifacts. I tested four and rejected two of them honestly:

REJECTED 1 — builder averages the wrong quantity. deriveSeries pools individual (code, year, month) rows and takes their MEAN, rather than summing across a slug's HS codes within each (year, month) and then averaging across years. For the 18 panel slugs mapped to more than one code this is the wrong estimator in principle. Empirically it is nearly inert: recomputing both ways flips exactly ONE argmax (cherry-tomato, month 1 -> month 12, a one-month shift). Not the explanation.

REJECTED 2 — nominal-value trend plus a partial final year would bias which months carry an extra high-value observation. Checked: 66 of 67 reconstructible panel series end at 2025-12, one at 2024-12. No partial-year imbalance. Not the explanation.

PARTIAL — non-independence. 5 import vectors are shared by 2 slugs each (beef-tenderloin/striploin on the same two boneless-loin lines, onion/red-onion on 070310, lemon/lime on 080550, red-potato/russet-potato on 070190, green-leaf/red-leaf lettuce on the two seasonal lettuce lines), so 68 slugs carry only 63 distinct import calendars and 10 of the 68 pairs are definitionally incapable of tracking a slug-specific price calendar. Dropping all 10 leaves the pooled result null (n=58, diff -0.086, p2 = 0.922), so this modestly loosens the stated MDE but does not itself change the conclusion.

CONFIRMED — the vintage split, detailed in fatalProblem. This one both fits better than the finding's own interpretation and reproduces the observed statistic exactly as a cancellation. Under my lens's stated rule ("if a boring explanation fits as well as the interesting one, this must be killed or heavily caveated"), a boring explanation that fits strictly BETTER is a kill.

I held myself to the same hostile standard on the rescue. Neither subgroup clears 0.05 after even Bonferroni over the two subsets (0.098 -> ~0.20; 0.072 -> ~0.14), so I am NOT asserting a signal exists. The <10y arm's +0.821 is almost certainly noise from argmaxes computed on 3 annual observations per calendar month. And the >=10y arm is confounded with commodity class (HS6-level counter-seasonal produce plus pork cuts) rather than being a clean data-quality contrast, so even its point estimate cannot be attributed to history length alone. Restricting the long arm to produce only weakens it further (n=35, diff -0.486, p2 = 0.279). All of that argues for kill, not for flipping the finding.

What should survive as a handback is not a finding but a data-quality defect: cost-index/ingredient-state-record.json is a published CC-BY download whose `import_seasonal_index` field ships 3-year and 16-year estimation windows side by side with nothing on the row telling a consumer which they are holding, and with date-windowed HTS lines producing unbalanced month coverage on the short ones. A reader comparing cherry-tomato's seasonal index to banana's is comparing 3 observations per month against 16. That is worth fixing (add an `import_index_years` / `import_index_span` field, or suppress the index below a minimum-years threshold the way seasonality.json already suppresses months below minYearsPerMonth=2) and it is the honest yield of this investigation.
kills.requiredCaveat: If the panel overrides the kill and publishes anyway, the null MUST NOT be stated as a property of the import calendar, and the following must accompany it in the body rather than as footnotes: (1) The 68-slug panel is not one population. Splitting on import-series history length — a boundary set by when the underlying Census codes entered this repo's pull, not by any analyst choice — gives diff = -0.700 (n=40, p=0.098) on slugs with 14-16 years of import history and diff = +0.821 (n=28, p=0.072) on slugs with 3-4 years. Their weighted average is the published -0.074. The aggregate null is a cancellation of two opposite-signed halves, not evidence that the calendars are unrelated. (2) The sentence "rules out any true phase advantage larger than about one month in either direction" must be struck; it is false at the subgroup level, where the point estimates are 0.70 and 0.82 months in opposite directions. (3) "Refuted" must be replaced with "not established": recomputing the import index on the same 5-year window seasonality.json uses (2021-2025) — the commensurability standard Muntin already applies to its own edition spine — yields diff = -0.900, p = 0.0316 in the predicted direction on the long-history subset. (4) State plainly that 23 of the 68 slugs carry a 12-month "seasonal index" estimated from 3-4 annual observations per calendar month, several from date-windowed HTS tariff lines with unbalanced per-month coverage (cherry-tomato: [8,8,12,12,12,12,22,22,22,22,24,24] observations by month), and that the argmax of such a series is not a measurement of seasonality. (5) State that 10 of the 68 slugs (beef-tenderloin/striploin, onion/red-onion, lemon/lime, red-potato/russet-potato, green-leaf/red-leaf lettuce) share an import calendar with another panel slug and therefore cannot track a slug-specific price calendar by construction — 68 rows carry only 63 distinct import calendars. (6) Note that any signal in the long-history arm would restate the published ERS fact that US produce imports peak in the northern winter when domestic supply is absent, so that arm is not novel either.

kills.reasoning:
All three layers of this finding are prior art, and the layer the analyst promotes as the "real" discovery is not even an empirical fact — it is arithmetic.

LAYER 1 — the pre-registered episodic claim (raw 36.56% vs 24.85%, 1.47x, p=0.0001). The analyst already refutes it internally (84.0% mechanical; conditional excess 1.88pp at p=0.12–0.14; INVERTS to −2.31pp, p=0.986 in the lock bucket that the claim is about). Independently, the raw uncorrected form is the single most-published result in the conformal literature. Gibbs & Candes, "Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift" (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv 2106.00170) demonstrates precisely this: non-adaptive conformal fails to cover Fannie Mae realized volatility through the 2008 crisis while adaptive does not. Barber, Candes, Ramdas & Tibshirani, "The limits of distribution-free conditional predictive inference" (Info. & Inference 10:455–482, 2021) proves that exact conditional coverage is IMPOSSIBLE distribution-free — i.e. "coverage does not hold uniformly across time" is a theorem, not a discovery. The entire ACI/EnbPI/SPCI/Bellman-CI literature exists because of this. Dead twice over.

LAYER 2 — the post-hoc onset variant (event ±4wk, 13.30pp conditional excess). Post hoc (1 of 5 windows), not de-tautologized by the analyst's own caveat #2 (absolute step size does not condition on step-relative-to-trailing-sigma, which IS the definition of a miss). And it is textbook: "coverage collapses at a regime change, then recovers as the rolling calibration window absorbs it" is the motivating observation of change-point conformal (openreview.net/pdf/693af6b1ea916c95c110b1383d0c7df5c45182ba) and of regime-aware calibration, which literature reports lifting standard volatility-scaled conformal from 76.5% to 94.6% empirical coverage. The analyst's own mechanism sentence ("consistent with the band adapting inside its 26-week residual window") is a restatement of the published motivation.

LAYER 3 — the promoted "robust, non-tautological" finding (mean 74.64%, pooled 74.47%, 62/63 below nominal, 52/63 CI entirely below, 0 above). THIS IS THE FATAL ONE. I read /home/user/potentially-profitable/tools/_shared/cost-conformal.js lines 44–50: `quantile()` is the plain type-7 INTERPOLATED empirical quantile over the sorted last-`window` residuals. There is NO split-conformal finite-sample correction — no ⌈(1−α/2)(n+1)⌉ order statistic. Shipped defaults (confirmed lines ~148–152, and the finding's own provenance says build-cost-lockfloat.mjs passes default opts): alpha=0.20, window=26, minResid=8. I re-implemented that exact `quantile()` byte-for-byte and measured its coverage on IID EXCHANGEABLE residuals — no volatility clustering, no distribution shift, no food prices whatsoever: window=26 gives 74.75% (Gaussian) and 74.55% (t3), against nominal 80.00%. Shorter windows give 69.14% (W=13) and 64.39% (W=8), which is what the early steps of each replay use. Observed: 74.47% pooled, 74.64% mean per item. The match is within ~0.3pp. Order-statistic algebra agrees: naive upper sits near the 22.5th of 27, lower near the 3.5th of 27, span ≈ 70–75%. So the band is an ~74.7% band BY CONSTRUCTION. "62 of 63 items below nominal, 52 of 63 with CI entirely below, 0 above" is exactly what a deterministic ~5.3pp estimator bias applied to every item must produce. It would reproduce on 63 series of white noise. It says nothing about food prices, about the 63 ingredients, or about the instrument's market behavior. The correction itself is textbook split conformal — the coverage bound γ ≤ P(S_{n+1} ≤ q̂) < γ + 1/(n+1) holds only with the ⌈(1−α)(n+1)⌉ index; that IS the published content.

INTERNAL PRIOR ART compounds it. cost-conformal.js already ships an ACI-style widening path whose trigger condition is literally `if (opts.calibrate && pointRate != null && pointRate < nominal)` — the author coded the remedy for the exact case reported here as a discovery. build-cost-lockfloat.mjs gates lock on `coverageLo >= LOCK_MIN_COVERLO` = 0.60, a threshold that only makes sense if you already assume realized coverage sits well under 0.80. And docs/cost-index-ux-plan.md carries two standing action items — "Render a reliability visual on the methodology page (nominal 80% vs realized 83%)" and "Distinguish nominal (80%) from realized (83%) explicitly wherever both appear." The nominal-vs-realized gap is a pre-existing, documented, scheduled-to-publish item. (The 83% there is stale and belongs to a different surface — cost-confidence-calibration.json / cost-index-calibration-report.json, not cost-lockfloat.json — which is a real errata item, but errata is not discovery.)

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, and it is not a finding: a one-line implementation defect. A surface labeled an "80% band" is structurally a ~74.7% band. That is worth an ADR and a fix (use ⌈(1−α/2)(n+1)⌉, or equivalently clamp the quantile level to (1−α/2)(n+1)/n). It is a bug ticket for the operator, high value internally, zero value as a published discovery — and publishing it as "we measured our band and it undercovers" would itself be a small honesty failure, since the honest statement is "we omitted the finite-sample correction and our band was never an 80% band."

No trade-press, USDA ERS, BLS, or Technomic/Circana/CoBank source is needed to kill this; the statistics literature and the repo's own source file are sufficient. (For completeness I did check USDA ERS Food Price Outlook forecast-evaluation material and agricultural-econometrics interval literature; nothing there contradicts the above, and ERS's own prediction-interval documentation confirms interval reliability under volatility is an openly discussed, non-novel problem.)

Uncertain-defaults-to-kill does not even apply here — I am not uncertain. The promoted headline reproduces on Gaussian noise.
kills.fatalProblem: The finding's own promoted headline — "against an 80% nominal, mean coverage 74.64%, 62 of 63 below, 52 of 63 with CI entirely below, 0 above" — is not a measurement of the market, it is a property of the estimator. cost-conformal.js (lines 44–50) computes the band with the plain type-7 interpolated empirical quantile over the last 26 residuals, omitting the split-conformal finite-sample correction ⌈(1−α/2)(n+1)⌉. Re-running that exact function on IID EXCHANGEABLE residuals with the shipped defaults (alpha=0.20, window=26) yields 74.75% coverage on Gaussian and 74.55% on t3 — versus the observed 74.47% pooled / 74.64% mean. The "discovery" reproduces on white noise to within 0.3pp; it would appear identically on 63 series of coin flips. The undercoverage is therefore known textbook content (the γ ≤ P < γ + 1/(n+1) bound), not an empirical result, and it is already coded around inside the repo (the `pointRate < nominal` ACI-widening branch, and the lock gate set at coverageLo ≥ 0.60 rather than 0.80). Separately, the two episodic layers are the canonical published results of Gibbs & Candes (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv 2106.00170 — non-adaptive conformal loses coverage through the 2008 volatility episode) and Barber/Candes/Ramdas/Tibshirani (Info. & Inference 10:455–482, 2021 — distribution-free conditional coverage is provably impossible), and the primary one is refuted by the analyst's own tautology control anyway (conditional excess 1.88pp, p=0.12–0.14, inverting to −2.31pp/p=0.986 in the lock bucket).
kills.requiredCaveat: Do not publish this as a finding in any form. kills.reasoning:
I attacked novelty on four fronts. Three of them land hard.

(1) THE STATISTICAL HEADLINE IS A KNOWN METHODOLOGICAL ARTIFACT, NOT A DISCOVERY. The finding's own probe already falsifies the mechanism (collapsed 3-layer test D3=7 vs null [4,10], p=0.567). What remains — "D=21 vs null95=7 because the missing sets are perfectly nested (SEASON ⊂ EVENTS ⊂ BAND)" — is textbook monotone missingness: a missing-data pattern is monotone when variables can be ordered so that missing one implies missing all subsequent ones, and it is standard that it arises from logical/technical constraints between measurements (here, three layers computed off one file, data/cost-index-history.json). The missing-data literature explicitly documents that co-clustering diagnostics on missingness indicators become misleading under a monotone pattern and that one must check for an underlying monotone structure before reading the clustering as informative (CRAN smdi "Multivariate missingness and monotonicity"; arXiv 2411.03848 "Monotone Missing Data: A Blessing and a Curse"). So the permutation result rediscovers a documented artifact class. Not novel, and not about food data.

(2) MECHANISM A — 16 OF THE 21 ITEMS — IS AN 88-YEAR-OLD PUBLISHED JURISDICTIONAL FACT, AND ITS FRAMING IS CONTRADICTED BY THE PUBLIC RECORD ITSELF. That seafood carries no USDA AMS wholesale reference is not a gap anyone discovered; it is the reason NOAA's Fishery Market News exists — the program opened in New York City on 14 Feb 1938 under Commerce/NMFS, and AMS's seafood role is grades and standards, not Market News prices (ams.usda.gov/grades-standards/fish-seafood vs fisheries.noaa.gov Fishery Market News). Worse for the claim: NOAA's public seafood record is DEEPER than the panel's, not thinner. NOAA/NEFSC publishes daily New England auction prices, daily Boston lobster prices (except Wednesday), weekly New York frozen prices (Friday) and weekly Boston frozen prices (Wednesday), with the online archive hosted at NEFSC covering 2014 and newer, exportable to spreadsheet. The finding's "9–10 monthly observations spanning 2025-02→2026-04" is therefore the ingestion footprint of this instrument (a monthly roll-up begun Feb 2025), not a limit of the public record. Publishing those 15 seafood slugs as items "the public record cannot describe" would be factually wrong and falsifiable in one click by any reader who opens nefsc.noaa.gov/read/socialsci/marketNews.php. The finding's own caveat 2 half-concedes this ("'dark' here partly means 'recently added to this panel'") but the revisedClaim still asserts they "have no AMS wholesale reference series at all" as if that were the public record's fact rather than an agency-boundary fact plus an ingest choice.

(3) THE BROADER GENRE — "the public food-price record has enumerable gaps" — IS THOROUGHLY DOCUMENTED, INCLUDING BY THE AGENCIES THEMSELVES, WITH QUANTIFIED SUPPRESSION. CRS R48589 (2025), "U.S. Retail Food Price Data: FAQs and Issues for Congress," discusses AMS reporting gaps and the limits of federal food price data directly. The National Academies' "A Consumer Food Data System for 2030 and Beyond" (2020) is an entire consensus report on gaps in the federal food data system. AMS publishes its own suppression rule and its arithmetic: under the pre-2001 confidentiality guideline USDA estimated ~30% of daily swine and cattle reports were withheld, versus under 2% under 3/70/20 — a published, quantified coverage-failure census. AMS also publicly documents thin-market non-publication (e.g., no daily carcass lamb reports where 3/70/20 cannot be met). ERS documents that it collects no price data itself and inherits others' coverage. What I could NOT find published anywhere is a per-ingredient coverage matrix for a restaurant catalog — no ERS, BLS, AMS, FAO/GIEWS, Mintec, Datassential, Technomic or CoBank product publishes "for THIS item, here is which of five layers exists." That residual novelty is real but modest, and it is largely a novelty of packaging a known class of fact for an audience, not a new fact.

(4) INTERNAL PRIOR ART MAKES IT SMALLER STILL, AND CREATES A LIVE CONTRADICTION. /home/user/potentially-profitable/blog/cost-index-2026-07/index.html already publishes the catalog-level version: "withholds 73 ... the 73 withholds split no-series 61, volatile 5, monthly-thin 4, flat 3," and "39 of 100 tracked ingredients qualify, 61 are still building history." So the mechanism census is already a published Muntin surface; only the per-slug reason is unpublished (the public lock-float mirror strips it). And those live numbers do not reconcile with the finding's measured marginals from the current files — BAND withhold 37 (not 73) and SEASON ready 84 (not 39), three weeks apart on the same 100-item catalog. Any publication built on 37/84 silently contradicts a live page unless the swing is explained.

(5) WHAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES IS 5 HERBS, AND IT IS UNVERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE. I confirmed the raw series myself: rosemary is 750¢ for 96 of 130 weeks and 850¢ for 34 (two levels, 2024-01-10→2026-06-30, source usda-ams-boston); basil has 6 levels; thyme 7. I found no publication measuring distinct-level counts in USDA terminal herb quotes, so as a measurement this is plausibly novel. But it is an instance of a documented class — reported-price rigidity and slow adjustment in USDA Market News is established in ag econ (the AMS cattle price-reporting study finding reported prices do not adjust to changing conditions fast enough, with evidence of selective reporting; the 2023 Food Policy critique of boxed-beef reporting being essentially unchanged for two decades), and terminal reports print "market steady" as their default state. And the interpretation ("an administered, effectively non-varying print") is an inference about USDA's reporting drawn from ONE extracted integer per week, where the underlying Boston terminal report prints per-package, per-origin values and ranges. I could not verify against the raw report — ams.usda.gov PDFs and the mirror sites both returned 403 from this environment. Per the finding's own caveat 3, removing the 16 leaves D=5, which is exactly the testSpec's "falsified if D < 5" boundary: one ingredient of slack.

NET: the headline is falsified by the finding's own probe and is a rediscovered monotone-missingness artifact; the dominant mechanism (16/21) is a published 1938 agency boundary whose "dark" framing is contradicted by NOAA's daily/weekly Boston–NY archive back to 2014; the genre is covered by CRS, the National Academies, and AMS's own suppression documentation; the catalog-level version is already on Muntin's own blog with different numbers. The only unpublished residue is a 5-item herb rigidity note sitting on the kill boundary and unverified against the primary quote. That is context and an ingestion bug report, not a discovery. Default-kill applies.

keyFindings: MECHANISM (Q1): the unfalsifiable claim is the OPTIMUM under the training objective, not a bug. Kalai/Nachum/Vempala/Zhang, Why Language Models Hallucinate (arXiv 2509.04664), show hallucination is a classification error forced by pretraining statistics plus post-training incentives: binary 0/1 grading penalizes abstention, so guessing strictly dominates saying I-don't-know. Corollary for insight generation: a hedged, mechanism-free claim is simultaneously maximum-plausibility AND unscoreable-as-wrong. If the reward is 'produce an insight', the gradient points at slop. Hedging vocabulary is the diagnostic surface marker precisely because hedging IS the linguistic act of deleting the truth condition.

EXHORTATION MAKES IT WORSE — the most operationally important finding. Peters & Chin-Yee, Royal Society Open Science 12(4):241776 (2025): LLM summaries of scientific papers overgeneralized in 26-73% of cases, were ~5x more likely than human-written summaries to contain broad generalizations, NEWER models were worse than older, and when explicitly prompted to avoid inaccuracies models were nearly TWICE as likely to overgeneralize. A prose instruction telling the generator to be rigorous is not a control; it is an anti-control. Only mechanical rejection counts.

SYCOPHANCY IS THE SECOND MECHANISM AND IS NEAR-TOTAL BY DEFAULT. npj Digital Medicine (2025), When helpfulness backfires: five frontier LLMs showed up to 100% initial compliance with logically incoherent medical requests, prioritizing helpfulness over consistency. What fixed it: explicit permission to reject the request, a factual-recall cue, and small-scale SFT — rejection rates rose without hurting general benchmarks. Applied here: 'find an interesting finding in this data' is itself the incoherent request when the slice contains nothing. The generator must have a rewarded, logged NO-FINDING output or it will manufacture one.

PRE-EXECUTION 'INTERESTINGNESS' IS ANTI-PREDICTIVE. Si, Hashimoto & Yang, The Ideation-Execution Gap (arXiv 2506.20803, ICLR 2026): 43 expert researchers each spent 100+ hours executing randomly assigned LLM-generated vs human-generated research ideas. LLM ideas won on pre-execution novelty ratings; after execution their scores dropped significantly more on every metric (novelty, excitement, effectiveness, overall; p<0.05) and the ranking FLIPPED so human ideas scored higher. Ranking candidate findings by how interesting they sound, before verification, actively selects the worst ones.

QUANTIFIED STATISTICAL DAMAGE (Q2). Baumann, Rottger et al., Large Language Model Hacking (arXiv 2509.08825): 13 million labels, 18 models, 37 annotation tasks from 21 published studies, 2,361 realistic hypotheses. Incorrect statistical conclusions in ~31% of hypotheses for state-of-the-art models and ~50% for small models. Error rate approaches 70% when the p-value sits near 0.05. Variance decomposition: task characteristics ~21%, model capability ~8%, prompt engineering <1%. You cannot prompt-engineer out of this; only human-verified labels and correction estimators help, and the estimators trade Type I for Type II error.

LLMs SPECIFICALLY MISS SUBGROUP STRUCTURE. CausalPitfalls / Ice Cream Doesn't Cause Drowning (arXiv 2505.13770): LLMs are especially susceptible to Simpson's and Berkson's paradoxes because they over-rely on surface correlations and POOLED/aggregate statistics while neglecting subgroup structure, and they deliver the wrong causal conclusion confidently. The benchmark separates direct prompting from code-assisted prompting (model writes executable statistical analysis) and treats them as materially different reliability regimes.

EXECUTION FIXES ARITHMETIC, NOT INFERENCE. StatABench (arXiv 2606.22977): best model reaches only 68.6% on closed statistical questions; advanced agent frameworks score 61.86/100 on open-ended modeling. Errors are dominated by inappropriate TOOL/TEST SELECTION and RESULT INTERPRETATION, plus a measured 'tool-integration tax' when translating concepts into operations. So a code-execution sandbox is necessary but nowhere near sufficient — the wrong test, correctly executed, is the dominant slop path.

BASE-RATE NEGLECT PERSISTS AT ROUGHLY HUMAN RATES, AND HAS A KNOWN FIX. Comparative studies put ChatGPT at ~50% on base-rate-neglect items vs ~56% for humans, and conjunction-fallacy performance in the same band. Chain-of-thought partially mitigates but does not eliminate probabilistic errors. Natural-frequency framing (counts, not percentages) measurably reduces base-rate neglect in both humans and LLMs — a free, implementable intervention.

SERIAL DEPENDENCE IS THE #1 KILLER FOR A PRICE PANEL. The Autocorrelation Blind Spot (arXiv 2604.14414) quantifies it: lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.928 means a 27x reduction in effective observations; rho above ~0.5 puts a metric at severe significance-inflation risk; the paper estimates 42% of naive pooled findings may be spurious. This is the modern restatement of Yule (1926) nonsense correlations and Granger-Newbold (1974) spurious regression: two trending or persistent series produce very high R-squared with no relationship, signalled by a low Durbin-Watson. Weekly commodity price series are exactly this regime.

VALUE, VOLUME AND PRICE ARE THREE DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE CONFUSION IS A KNOWN, NAMED BIAS. Unit value = value divided by quantity, so (a) small volumes explode the ratio, and (b) bias is 'mainly attributed to changes in the mix of heterogeneous items' — a composition effect masquerading as a price move. IMF XMPI ch.2, CEPII TradeUnitValues, and Diewert's Notes on Unit Value Index Bias all conclude unit-value indexes are known NOT to track price indexes. An index-level move with unchanged constituent prices is a weights/mix artifact, full stop.

MULTIPLICITY IS BIGGER THAN THE TESTS YOU RAN (Q4). Gelman & Loken, The Garden of Forking Paths (2013): the false-positive inflation comes from the analyses you COULD have run given the data, so counting executed tests undercounts. For a generative discovery engine this is actually good news — the engine enumerates its candidate space explicitly, so the true m is knowable and loggable, unlike in human research.

THE RIGHT CORRECTION FAMILY IS FDR, BUT DEPENDENCE FORCES PERMUTATION. Benjamini-Hochberg controls the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejections, is less stringent than FWER control, and is the industry standard for many-metric testing (Optimizely's Stats Engine uses a tiered BH across metrics and variations; standard practice splits metrics into primary/secondary/guardrail families and corrects within family). But BH assumes independence or PRDS. For the many-hypotheses-one-dataset case the rigorous literature is significant pattern mining: Tarone's testability correction (exploits discreteness, prunes untestable patterns, beats Bonferroni) and Westfall-Young max-T permutation, which accounts for inter-pattern dependence and achieves actual FWER approximately equal to alpha with higher power than Tarone (Llinares-Lopez et al., arXiv 1502.04315).

PRE-STUDY ODDS DOMINATE EVERYTHING. Ioannidis (PLoS Med 2005): PPV = (1-beta)R / ((1-beta)R + alpha), degraded further by bias u. The lever a discovery engine actually controls is R — the ratio of true to false relationships in the space it enumerates. Enumerating 10,000 candidate relations in a domain containing maybe 20 true ones sets R near zero, and no p-threshold rescues it. The corollary: a hypothesis BUDGET and a prior-plausibility filter are more powerful than any correction applied afterward.

ADAPTIVE SEARCH BURNS A PLAIN HOLDOUT ON THE FIRST PASS. Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold & Roth, The reusable holdout (Science 349:636, 2015): once hypotheses are chosen AFTER seeing the data, ordinary holdout validity collapses. Thresholdout uses differential-privacy noise to permit many adaptive holdout queries with a quantified degradation bound. A FunSearch-style engine is adaptive by construction, so this is the correct formal frame, not a nicety.

PRE-REGISTRATION HAS A LARGE MEASURED EFFECT AND GIVES YOU A CALIBRATION TARGET (Q3). Scheel, Schijen & Lakens (2021), 71 Registered Reports vs 152 standard reports in psychology: the first-tested hypothesis was supported in 44% of Registered Reports vs 96% of standard reports. That 44% is the honest hit rate for pre-registered exploratory work. A discovery engine reporting a 90% confirmation rate is reporting its search process, not its results.

SELF-CRITIQUE DOES NOT WORK; EXTERNAL, EXECUTABLE FEEDBACK DOES. Huang et al., LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (arXiv 2310.01798): intrinsic self-correction degrades performance because models cannot judge their own prior correctness. FlipFlop (arXiv 2311.08596): simply challenging a model flips correct answers to incorrect. Multi-agent debate does help factuality (Du et al.; A-HMAD rated +0.8 on a 5-point human factual-accuracy scale) but has two documented failure modes: confidently-wrong consensus, and persuasion override — CW-POR (arXiv 2504.00374) shows a single strategically persuasive adversarial agent can flip group outcomes. Debate must therefore be adjudicated by a re-runnable artifact, never by argument quality.

CITATIONS ARE NOT PROVENANCE. Across five LLM systems, citation accuracy ranged 0.791-0.873, i.e. 13-21% of generated citations were hallucinated; the RAG-grounded system scored highest (0.873); and providers that generate MORE citations achieved LOWER factual accuracy — a direct thoroughness/reliability trade-off. Displayed provenance must be machine-resolved and the cited number re-derived, or citation density becomes a slop amplifier rather than a gate.

ARTIFACT DISCRIMINATION HAS ESTABLISHED TOOLING (Q5). (a) Negative controls — Lipsitch, Tchetgen Tchetgen & Cohen, Epidemiology 21(3) 2010: a negative-control outcome shares every bias source with the real outcome but cannot be caused by the exposure; a hit on it indicts the pipeline, and the method detects confounding, selection bias, recall bias, immortal-time bias and analytic flaws. (b) Vintage artifacts — BLS revises 5 years of seasonally adjusted data annually, and the classic failure is that the move for the third month back is an artifact of differencing a revised level against an unrevised one (e.g. a reported 423,000 gain against a true 340,000). (c) Structural breaks — false break detection splits series into over-small intervals, adds parameters and overfits, so a detected break coinciding with a documented methodology change is presumptively an artifact. (d) Multiverse/specification curve (Ioannidis vibration of effects 2008; Simonsohn et al. 2020) reports the distribution of the effect over all defensible specifications rather than one.
implementableRules: R1 TYPED FINDING RECORD. Every candidate lives in data/findings.json (or .jsonl) with required fields: id, claim (one sentence), metric (exact derivation path), population (series set + date window), transform, test (named statistic + script path), effect (point estimate + CI), nEffective, familyId, killCondition, preRegisteredAt, testedAt, provenance[] (sourceId + vintage + retrievedAt), status in {proposed,tested,confirmed,withheld,killed,artifact}. A record missing killCondition, or with preRegisteredAt >= testedAt, fails CI. This is the discovery-engine analogue of sourced-claims.json.

R2 EXECUTABLE KILL CONDITION. killCondition is not prose — it is {script, args, expect} returning a boolean. check-findings.mjs re-runs every confirmed finding's kill predicate against current data on every CI run; a true return auto-flips status to killed and the renderer drops it from every surface. A finding nobody can kill is not a finding.

R3 BAN UNFALSIFIABLE GRAMMAR MECHANICALLY. New gate check-finding-grammar.mjs, reusing the existing voice-contract banned-words machinery, rejects any claim string containing: may, might, could, suggests, tends to, often, can be, appears to, points to, hints at, signals, underscores, highlights, it is worth noting, while this may vary. Positively require in every claim: a number, a unit, a named population, and a date window. Hedging is the surface form of a deleted truth condition (Peters & Chin-Yee; slop-detection literature).

R4 REQUIRE THE PRINTABLE NEGATION. Each record carries wouldHaveSaid — the exact sentence the engine would have printed had the test gone the other way. If the generator cannot state it, the claim has no direction and no truth condition. Cheap to implement, catches directionless insight-shaped text immediately.

R5 NO MODEL-READ NUMBERS. Every digit in claim must be re-derivable by the same code path that produced effect. check-findings.mjs recomputes and diffs against the printed digit; any mismatch is fail-CI. This closes the transcription channel that would otherwise be spoken aloud by the audio renderer in EN+ES.

R6 REWARDED NO-FINDING OUTPUT. The generator's contract must include an explicit, first-class NO_FINDING return for a slice, and the ledger must show it being used at a nontrivial rate. If a run returns zero NO_FINDINGs across many slices, fail the run. (Direct implementation of the npj sycophancy fix: explicit permission to reject.)

R7 LOG THE ENUMERATION, NOT THE REPORT. The engine appends one line per hypothesis ENUMERATED to data/findings-ledger.jsonl, whether tested, withheld, or discarded. The m used for multiplicity correction is the ledger count for that run, never the count of survivors. Publish confirmed/enumerated on the methods page.

R8 CORRECT WITHIN DECLARED FAMILIES. data/findings-families.json declares families (seasonality, co-movement, event-coincidence, yield, basket-composition, vendor-spread). Correct within family. A finding may never migrate families after testing. Mirrors the primary/secondary/guardrail split that experimentation platforms use with tiered BH.

R9 CORRECTION METHOD BY TIER. Exploratory tier: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at q=0.10. Anything promoted to a dispatch or an evergreen surface: q=0.05. Because hypotheses drawn from one price panel are strongly dependent, either use Benjamini-Yekutieli (the sum-1/i penalty) or, preferred, Westfall-Young max-T permutation over the enumerated family — WY accounts for the dependence structure and achieves actual FWER approximately alpha with more power than Tarone/Bonferroni. Store the method name and the corrected threshold on every record.

R10 HARD HYPOTHESIS BUDGET, DECLARED BEFORE THE RUN. Set maxHypotheses per family in config. Exceeding it ABORTS the run rather than silently truncating the ledger. Rationale: Ioannidis PPV is driven by pre-study odds R, and R is set by how wide you let the enumeration go — no threshold rescues an unbounded search.

R11 PRIOR-PLAUSIBILITY FILTER, RECORDED BEFORE TESTING. Each candidate must either name a pre-existing mechanism from data/cost-index-drivers.json or an ADR, or be tagged exploratory:true. Exploratory candidates are held to the stricter q AND to mandatory holdout replication (R12). This raises R by construction, which is the highest-leverage lever available.

R12 EXPLORE/CONFIRM TIME SPLIT. Partition the panel at a frozen date: the engine sees only explore. A finding is publishable only after re-clearing its PRE-REGISTERED threshold on the unseen confirm window. Store confirmWindow and confirmResult on the record. If the confirm window must be re-queried, implement Thresholdout (Dwork et al. 2015): return the holdout answer only when it differs from the explore answer by more than a noisy tolerance, charge a query budget, and abort the run when the budget is spent.

R13 SPECIFICATION MULTIVERSE, NOT ONE SPEC. Run the declared spec grid — log level vs log difference, deseasonalized vs raw, windows of 26/52/104 weeks, with and without the two most influential dates — and store sharePositive, shareSignificant, medianEffect. Gate: a finding whose SIGN flips across defensible specs is withheld, never published. Publish the specification-curve summary alongside the headline.

R14 NEVER CORRELATE LEVELS. transform=levels is not an allowed value for any co-movement or association finding. Test on log differences, or explicitly test and report cointegration. Refuse at the gate. (Granger-Newbold spurious regression; high R-squared with low Durbin-Watson is the signature.)

R15 EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE IS MANDATORY. Compute and store nEffective = n * (1 - rho1) / (1 + rho1), or use Newey-West / cluster-robust SEs with lag = ceil(n^(1/3)), and use nEffective in both the test and the printed CI. Gate: refuse any time-series finding where nEffective < 30, or where lag-1 rho > 0.5 and the test used naive n. (Autocorrelation Blind Spot: rho=0.928 costs 27x of your observations.)

R16 VALUE / VOLUME / PRICE SEPARATION. Any metric computed as value divided by quantity is tagged unitValue:true and MAY NOT be called a price in prose (extend the existing fabrication blocklist). Before publishing any unit-value move, run the fixed-weight recomputation (hold weights at t-1) and publish the split. If the fixed-weight recomputation kills the move, reclassify it as a composition finding, not a price finding.

R17 AGGREGATE MOVES REQUIRE CONSTITUENT ATTRIBUTION. Any index/basket-level claim carries a per-constituent contribution vector that sums to the headline move within tolerance, plus weightsVersion. If weightsVersion or basket membership changed inside the window, status=withheld with a stated reason — the exact rule the edition-commensurability logic already enforces for week-over-week.

R18 MANDATORY SIMPSON LOOP. For every claim, automatically compute the pooled estimate AND each declared stratum (season, region, source-agency, ingredient class). If any stratum's sign opposes the pooled sign, set simpson:true and force the STRATIFIED statement to be the headline. Do not ask the model to notice this; CausalPitfalls shows models do not volunteer subgroup structure.

R19 PRINT COUNTS NEXT TO RATES. Every record stores raw numerator and denominator; the renderer must print the natural-frequency form (in 7 of 41 weeks) adjacent to any percentage or probability. Natural-frequency framing measurably reduces base-rate neglect in both readers and models.

R20 BALANCED-PANEL / COVERAGE GUARD. Store seriesCoverage (contributing series count per period). Any coverage change greater than 5% inside the window forces status=withheld until the finding is recomputed on the balanced panel — series present in every period. This is the survivorship-bias gate: a basket that gained reporters looks like a market that moved.

R21 VINTAGE DISCIPLINE. Every observation carries vintage (release date of the print). Deltas may ONLY be computed within a single vintage; cross-vintage differencing is a hard CI failure. A finding that does not survive recomputation on the prior vintage is labeled artifact. (BLS third-month-back example is the canonical case: 423,000 reported vs 340,000 true.)

R22 BOUNDARY REGISTRY AND TEST. Maintain data/source-methodology-changes.json with dated entries for methodology changes, re-anchors, basket re-weights, seasonal-factor revisions, unit changes and fiscal boundaries. If a detected change point falls within plus-or-minus one period of any entry, auto-label suspect:boundary and require an agency source note before publication.

R23 TWO MANDATORY NEGATIVE CONTROLS, BOTH AUTOMATED. (a) PIPELINE control: run the identical detector on a series that shares the ingestion path but cannot share the claimed mechanism. (b) TIMING control: run the identical detector with event dates shifted by a fixed offset. A hit on either at equal-or-greater strength retires the finding as an artifact. Store both results on the record. (Lipsitch et al. 2010.)

R24 PERMUTATION NULL PRESERVING AUTOCORRELATION. For every co-movement or event-coincidence finding, run the detector on at least 1,000 phase-randomized or block-bootstrapped surrogates that preserve the series' autocorrelation structure, and report the empirical p. This is the only honest null for a serially-correlated panel, and it is the same machinery that implements Westfall-Young in R9 — build it once.

R25 FRAGILITY AND FORENSICS. Leave-one-out on dates and on constituent series: if removing any single date or series kills significance, status=fragile, not confirmed. Additionally flag runs of identical values (carry-forward), values at the source's default/sentinel, effects driven by two or fewer observations, and any effect implying a physical quantity outside recorded historical bounds.

R26 INDEPENDENT-PIPELINE CORROBORATION FOR PROMOTION. Nothing reaches a dispatch or evergreen surface without the same phenomenon appearing in a series built by a different agency or collection method (NASS vs AMS vs BLS vs EIA). Absent corroboration, publish only inside the exploratory surface with an explicit single-source label. Store corroboration[] on the record.

R27 SEPARATE SEATS, SEPARATE SESSIONS. The generator never grades its own output. The critic runs in a FRESH context, receives only the record, the data and the code path — never the generator's framing or rationale — and returns pass/fail on named executable checks, not prose. (Intrinsic self-correction degrades performance; FlipFlop shows challenge alone flips correct answers.)

R28 ADJUDICATE BY ARTIFACT, NEVER BY ARGUMENT. If an adversarial or panel step is used, each side's position must be attached to a re-runnable script whose exit code decides the outcome. Prose-only critique is inadmissible. (CW-POR: one confident persuasive agent can override truth in LLM debate.)

R29 RANK BY COMPUTED QUANTITIES ONLY. The publication queue is ordered by a deterministic score over effect size, nEffective, corroboration count and specification-curve stability. No model-assigned interestingness, novelty or surprise score may enter the ranking. (Ideation-Execution Gap: pre-execution novelty ratings inverted after execution.)

R30 THE NEGATIVE PATH IS A SHIPPED SURFACE. Every run publishes its killed, withheld, fragile and artifact records with machine-written reasons to a public listing (e.g. /open/findings/ filtered by status). Withholding must cost the engine nothing and publishing must cost it something — the reverse of the default incentive.

R31 CONFIRMATION-RATE CIRCUIT BREAKER. If a run's confirmed/enumerated ratio exceeds 0.5, FAIL the run and force a ledger audit. The registered-report benchmark for honest pre-registered work is 44% support for the first-tested hypothesis versus 96% without pre-registration; a discovery engine claiming a 90% hit rate is reporting its search, not its results.

R32 HUMAN SEAT IS A VETO, NOT AN AUTHOR SEAT. Same shape as the existing editor's-note contract: the operator may kill a finding or add prose context, may NOT add a number, may NOT introduce an ingredient, and may NOT upgrade a withheld record to confirmed. Enforced by check-findings.mjs diffing the human layer against the machine record.

R33 CALIBRATION LEDGER — THE ONLY RULE THAT PROVES THE REST. Each published finding stores checkBackAt. A scheduled job re-runs its kill predicate on the horizon date and appends the outcome to data/findings-calibration.json. Publish the running hit rate, by family, on the methods page. This converts the system from asserting rigor to demonstrating it, and makes overclaiming expensive rather than free.

R34 PROVENANCE MUST RESOLVE AND RECOMPUTE. Every provenance entry stores sourceId, url, vintage, retrievedAt and the exact query/series id. The gate resolves the reference and re-derives the cited number; a stored citation that cannot be re-derived is fail-CI, not a warning. Do not let citation DENSITY stand in for citation validity — measured citation accuracy across systems runs 0.791-0.873, and providers generating more citations scored lower on factual accuracy.

R35 REGISTER RESEARCH CLAIMS ONLY FROM PRIMARY TEXT. Every number in this spec was obtained from search-engine summaries of the source papers; WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on every domain in this container. Before any of these figures enters data/sourced-claims.json or any published prose, retrieve the primary PDF on the operator's Mac and verify the number in situ. Treat this spec's numbers as leads, not as gated claims.
